--[[
	Lightning/PDataBuilder  -  per-bolt pData construction shared by Emit + Animate.
	Split from Lightning/init (500-line cap). Rolls every per-bolt range, composes
	the launch frame (RotXYZ + DirMode + Spread), samples spawn Pos/Shape, and seeds
	the origin-motion state. emitCtx carries per-burst EmitIndex/EvenOffset fields
	for even-distribution sampling.
]]

local GraphMod = require(script.Parent.Parent.Graph)
local RangeMod = require(script.Parent.Parent.Range)
local AxisLinksMod = require(script.Parent.Parent.AxisLinks)
local Constants = require(script.Parent.Parent.PartConstants)
local TurbulenceMod = require(script.Parent.Parent.Turbulence)
local EndpointsMod = require(script.Parent.Endpoints)

local DirectionVectors = Constants.DirectionVectors

local PDataBuilder = {}

-- Flat-zero sequences (the writeDefaults stamp) count as "no graph" so idle
-- emitters skip the per-frame motion accumulation entirely.
function PDataBuilder.liveGraph(seq)
	if not seq then return nil end
	if GraphMod.IsStatic(seq) and GraphMod.GetStaticValue(seq, 0) == 0 then return nil end
	return seq
end

-- Static-white ColorSequence (the writeDefaults stamp) counts as "no gradient"
-- so default bolts keep the single-color fast path.
function PDataBuilder.liveColor(seq)
	if not seq or typeof(seq) ~= "ColorSequence" then return nil end
	local kp = seq.Keypoints
	if #kp <= 1 then
		local c = kp[1] and kp[1].Value
		if not c or (c.R > 0.999 and c.G > 0.999 and c.B > 0.999) then return nil end
	end
	return seq
end

-- Flat-one Taper profile (the writeDefaults stamp) counts as "no taper" so the
-- per-roll width pass is skipped.
function PDataBuilder.liveProfile(seq)
	if not seq or typeof(seq) ~= "NumberSequence" then return nil end
	if GraphMod.IsStatic(seq) and GraphMod.GetStaticValue(seq, 0) == 1 then return nil end
	return seq
end

function PDataBuilder.build(item, data, model, rig, lifeTime, emitCtx)
	-- Normalize motion graphs BEFORE seeding/aliasing so downstream flags see nil.
	data.ThicknessProfile = PDataBuilder.liveProfile(data.ThicknessProfile)
	data.Speed = PDataBuilder.liveGraph(data.Speed)
	data.PosOffsetX = PDataBuilder.liveGraph(data.PosOffsetX)
	data.PosOffsetY = PDataBuilder.liveGraph(data.PosOffsetY)
	data.PosOffsetZ = PDataBuilder.liveGraph(data.PosOffsetZ)
	data.Turbulence = TurbulenceMod.isLive(data.Turbulence)
	local seeds = {
		Brightness = GraphMod.GenerateSeed(data.Brightness),
		Transparency = GraphMod.GenerateSeed(data.Transparency),
		Thickness = GraphMod.GenerateSeed(data.Thickness),
		ThicknessProfile = GraphMod.GenerateSeed(data.ThicknessProfile),
		Timescale = GraphMod.GenerateSeed(data.Timescale),
		Speed = GraphMod.GenerateSeed(data.Speed),
		PosOffsetX = GraphMod.GenerateSeed(data.PosOffsetX),
		PosOffsetY = GraphMod.GenerateSeed(data.PosOffsetY),
		PosOffsetZ = GraphMod.GenerateSeed(data.PosOffsetZ),
		Turbulence = GraphMod.GenerateSeed(data.Turbulence),
	}
	-- Linked graph axes (PosOffset) adopt the primary's graph + seed.
	AxisLinksMod.applyGraphAxisAliases(data, seeds, data.AxisLinks)
	local accel = data.Acceleration or Vector3.zero
	local growthSpeed = RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.GrowthSpeed)
	local pData = {
		Type = "Lightning",
		VisualPart = model,
		_rig = rig,
		Events = data.Events,
		StartTime = os.clock(),
		TotalKeyFrames = math.max(1, data.TotalKeyFrames),
		CurrentStep = 0,
		LifeTime = lifeTime,
		PartLife = data.PartLife or 0,
		_sourceItem = item,

		Graphs = {
			Color = data.Color,
			Gradient = PDataBuilder.liveColor(data.Gradient),
			Brightness = data.Brightness,
			Transparency = data.Transparency,
			Thickness = data.Thickness,
			ThicknessProfile = data.ThicknessProfile,
			Timescale = data.Timescale,
			Speed = data.Speed,
			PosOffsetX = data.PosOffsetX,
			PosOffsetY = data.PosOffsetY,
			PosOffsetZ = data.PosOffsetZ,
			Turbulence = data.Turbulence,
		},
		Seeds = seeds,
		_effectiveElapsed = GraphMod.InitialEffectiveElapsed(data.Timescale, seeds.Timescale, lifeTime),

		_endpointMode = data.TargetMode == "Seek" and "Seek"
			or ((data.TargetMode == "Point" and data.Target and data.Target.Parent) and "Point" or "Directional"),
		_target = data.Target,
		-- The authored Link (Link section). A top-level bolt's origin rides it by LinkMode; a
		-- nested bolt rides its parent clone instead (Endpoints.resolveEndpoints).
		_userLink = data.Link,
		-- Carried by a Container or a Matte: its place on the parent clone (NestedEmit.keepPlace).
		_parentOffset = emitCtx and emitCtx._rigPlace or nil,
		LinkMode = data.LinkMode,
		LinkAxes = data.LinkAxes,
		_seekRadius = math.max(RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.SeekRadius), 1),
		_seekRetarget = data.SeekRetarget == true,
		_seekBias = math.clamp(data.SeekBias or 0, 0, 1),
		_retargetSpeed = math.max(data.RetargetSpeed or 0, 0),
		-- Seek fires OnHit from its own scan (fireSeekHit); the generic
		-- Events.afterUpdate raycast + Collision actions must skip this pData.
		_ownsOnHit = true,
		_length = math.max(0.1, RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.Length)),
		-- Bolt-shape ranges roll ONCE per bolt (variety across a burst; stable within a bolt).
		_segCount = math.clamp(math.floor(RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.SegmentCount) + 0.5), 2, rig.mainSegs),
		_amplitude = RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.Amplitude),
		_decay = RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.AmplitudeDecay),
		_forkChance = RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.ForkChance),
		_forkDepth = math.floor(RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.ForkDepth) + 0.5),
		_forkLenScale = RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.ForkLengthScale),
		_sag = RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.Sag),
		_sagShape = RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.SagShape),
		_shapeMode = data.ShapeMode or "Jitter",
		_scrollSpeed = RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.ScrollSpeed),
		_waves = math.max(0.25, RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.Waves)),
		_scrollPhase = 0,
		_noiseSeedA = math.random() * 1000,
		_noiseSeedB = 500 + math.random() * 1000,
		_jitterAccum = 0,
		_lSpeed = growthSpeed,
		_growReversed = growthSpeed < 0,
		_tipDist = 0,
		_revealPtr = 0,
		_nestedAlive = { true },

		-- Origin motion (Speed along launch dir + Acceleration + Drag) and PosOffset
		-- displacement graphs. Accumulated per frame in UpdateLightning; applied to
		-- the origin by resolveEndpoints each roll.
		_accel = accel,
		_drag = data.Drag or 0,
		_dispMode = data.DisplacementMode or "Global",
		_motionOffset = Vector3.zero,
		_motionAccelVel = Vector3.zero,
		_hasMotion = data.Speed ~= nil or accel.Magnitude > 0,
		_hasDisp = data.PosOffsetX ~= nil or data.PosOffsetY ~= nil or data.PosOffsetZ ~= nil,
		-- Origin turbulence: sampled per frame into _turbRaw by UpdateLightning,
		-- applied by resolveEndpoints in the _dispMode frame.
		_hasTurb = data.Turbulence ~= nil,
		_turbFreq = data.TurbulenceFrequency or 1,
		_turbSeed = math.random() * 997 + 0.5,
		_turbRaw = nil,
	}
	local jitterHz = RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.JitterRate)
	pData._jitterInterval = jitterHz > 0 and 1 / jitterHz or math.huge

	-- Directional launch axis in SOURCE-local space: EmissionDirection rotated by
	-- RotXYZ (even-distribution aware) ± SpreadAngle. Spawn Pos offsets the origin
	-- in the origin frame (PosMode Global = world axes); applied live per roll by
	-- resolveEndpoints so moving sources/links carry the pattern.
	local dirInfo = DirectionVectors[data.EmissionDirection] or DirectionVectors[Enum.NormalId.Top]
	local localAxis = CFrame.new()[dirInfo.vector] * dirInfo.multiplier
	local spread = data.SpreadAngle or Vector2.new(0, 0)
	local rotS = AxisLinksMod.sampleRangeAxes(data, data.AxisLinks, {"RotX","RotY","RotZ"}, RangeMod, emitCtx)
	local rotXYZ = Constants.composeRotation(data.RotOrder or "Global", rotS.RotX or 0, rotS.RotY or 0, rotS.RotZ or 0)
	local cf = CFrame.lookAt(Vector3.zero, localAxis)
	-- Direction picks up RotXYZ only in DirMode=Local. RigidLocal (default) keeps the
	-- authored facing so Rot drives the Pos frame alone  -  rings keep their direction.
	if data.DirMode == "Local" then cf = cf * rotXYZ end
	if spread.X > 0 or spread.Y > 0 then
		cf = cf * CFrame.Angles(
			math.rad((math.random() * 2 - 1) * spread.X),
			math.rad((math.random() * 2 - 1) * spread.Y), 0)
	end
	pData._dirLocalVec = cf.LookVector
	pData._dirGlobal = data.DirMode == "Global"
	-- Rotation applies BEFORE position offsets (Part-emitter order): Local Pos +
	-- displacement frames live in the per-bolt ROTATED frame (rings/spirals).
	pData._originRot = rotXYZ
	local posS = AxisLinksMod.sampleRangeAxes(data, data.AxisLinks, {"PosX","PosY","PosZ"}, RangeMod, emitCtx)
	local px, py, pz = posS.PosX or 0, posS.PosY or 0, posS.PosZ or 0
	if px ~= 0 or py ~= 0 or pz ~= 0 then
		pData._originOffset = Vector3.new(px, py, pz)
		pData._originOffsetGlobal = data.PosMode == "Global"
	else
		pData._originOffset = nil
	end
	EndpointsMod.sampleShape(pData, data, item)
	return pData
end

return PDataBuilder

--[[
	Lightning/Rig  -  bolt Model + rig-buffer construction and pool acquire.
	Split from Lightning/init (500-line cap). Owns the weak-keyed Rigs map so
	buffers survive pool release/acquire cycles and gc with the model.
]]

local Pool = require(script.Parent.Parent.Pool)
local GraphMod = require(script.Parent.Parent.Graph)
local BoltGen = require(script.Parent.BoltGen)

local MAX_BOLT_PARTS = 64
local FAR_CFRAME = CFrame.new(1e9, 1e9, 1e9)

local Rig = {}

Rig.MAX_BOLT_PARTS = MAX_BOLT_PARTS
Rig.FAR_CFRAME = FAR_CFRAME

-- Weak-keyed by bolt Model.
Rig.Rigs = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

-- One segment part cloned from the RT. copyBare strips Transformed children (nested
-- source Part-Icles fire once per BOLT via NestedEmit.walk, never per segment).
-- Returns the first Decal/Texture child too: Transform hides RT decals (Transparency=1),
-- so writeVisuals must drive them alongside the part.
local function buildSegment(rt)
	local seg = Pool.copyBare(rt)
	seg.Anchored = true
	seg.CanCollide = false
	seg.CanQuery = false
	seg.CanTouch = false
	seg.Massless = true
	seg.Locked = true
	seg.Archivable = false
	seg.Transparency = 0
	local decal = seg:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Decal") or seg:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Texture")
	return seg, decal
end

-- Rig layout sizes for the range MAXIMUMS; each bolt rolls its own values within
-- them and parks unused slots at FAR_CFRAME.
function Rig.layoutFor(data)
	return BoltGen.layout(data.SegmentCount.Max, data.ForkDepth.Max, data.ForkChance.Max, MAX_BOLT_PARTS)
end

-- Fresh bolt Model + rig with every buffer pre-sized. Called on pool miss or when
-- the defensive rig check fails on a pool hit.
function Rig.buildRig(data)
	local partCount, mainSegs, forkSegs, forkSlots = Rig.layoutFor(data)
	local model = Instance.new("Model")
	model.Name = "LightningBolt"
	model.Archivable = false
	-- Consumed by EmitPointLight: nested lights fan out per segment on bolt Models.
	model:SetAttribute("_lightningBolt", true)
	local rig = {
		partCount = partCount, mainSegs = mainSegs,
		forkSegs = forkSegs, forkSlots = forkSlots,
		parts = table.create(partCount),
		rollCFs = table.create(partCount),
		writeCFs = table.create(partCount),
		segLen = table.create(partCount),
		revealDist = table.create(partCount),
		revealOrder = table.create(partCount),
		widthScale = table.create(partCount),
		decals = table.create(partCount),
		slotDepth = table.create(math.max(forkSlots, 1)),
		ptBuf = table.create(mainSegs + 1),
		basePtBuf = table.create(mainSegs + 1),
		forkPtBuf = table.create(forkSegs + 1),
		forkAnchorPos = {}, forkAnchorDir = {}, forkAnchorReveal = {},
		forkAnchorSlot = {}, forkAnchorPtIdx = {},
		-- Per-slot fork retention for scroll-mode re-anchoring (BoltGen.applyScrollForks).
		forkOriginIdx = {}, forkParentSlot = {}, forkParentPtIdx = {},
		forkLen = {}, forkU = {}, forkV = {}, forkSeedU = {}, forkSeedV = {},
		-- Taper bookkeeping (Rig.applyTaper): where each fork leaves its parent's arc.
		forkStartReveal = {}, forkStartFrac = {},
		forkLocalPts = {}, forkWorldPts = {},
		-- Skip-write caches (BoltGen.diffLive / planSizes).
		prevLive = table.create(partCount),
		lastWrittenLen = table.create(partCount),
		sizeWriteIdx = table.create(partCount),
		newlyLiveIdx = table.create(partCount),
		-- Per-part spatial Gradient sample, recomputed each roll (arc positions move).
		gradColor = table.create(partCount),
		-- Per-part Taper multiplier on Thickness, recomputed each roll.
		taper = table.create(partCount),
	}
	for slot = 1, forkSlots do
		rig.forkLocalPts[slot] = table.create(forkSegs + 1)
		rig.forkWorldPts[slot] = table.create(forkSegs + 1)
		rig.forkOriginIdx[slot] = 0
		rig.forkParentSlot[slot] = 0
	end
	-- Slot depth is fixed at build: first half depth 1, remainder depth 2. Width per
	-- part is a build-time constant (main = 1, forks scale by ForkLengthScale^depth).
	local depth1Slots = forkSlots > 0 and math.max(1, math.ceil(forkSlots / 2)) or 0
	for slot = 1, forkSlots do
		rig.slotDepth[slot] = slot <= depth1Slots and 1 or 2
	end
	-- Fork WIDTH decouples from ForkLengthScale with a floor: at small length scales
	-- length-coupled widths shrink forks to invisible hairlines (0.4² x 0.15-stud
	-- thickness = 0.024 studs).
	local lenScale = math.max(0.45, data.ForkLengthScale and data.ForkLengthScale.Max or 0.4)
	for i = 1, partCount do
		local seg, decal = buildSegment(data.RenderTemplate)
		seg.Name = "Seg" .. i
		seg.CFrame = FAR_CFRAME
		seg.Parent = model
		rig.parts[i] = seg
		rig.decals[i] = decal
		rig.rollCFs[i] = FAR_CFRAME
		rig.writeCFs[i] = FAR_CFRAME
		rig.segLen[i] = 0.05
		rig.revealDist[i] = math.huge
		rig.revealOrder[i] = i
		rig.prevLive[i] = false
		-- Sentinel: first planSizes write is unconditional per part.
		rig.lastWrittenLen[i] = -1
		rig.taper[i] = 1
		if i <= mainSegs then
			rig.widthScale[i] = 1
		else
			local slot = math.floor((i - mainSegs - 1) / forkSegs) + 1
			rig.widthScale[i] = lenScale ^ (rig.slotDepth[slot] or 1)
		end
	end
	Rig.Rigs[model] = rig
	return model, rig
end

-- Per-part width multiplier from the Taper profile (arc 0 = source, 1 = tip). Main parts read
-- their arc fraction of the main polyline; fork parts continue the parent's fraction at the
-- branch point to 1 over the fork's own length. A changed multiplier stamps the planSizes
-- force sentinel so the next flush resizes that part. No profile = every multiplier 1.
function Rig.applyTaper(rig, profile, seed, mainLen)
	local invMain = 1 / math.max(mainLen or 0, 1e-4)
	for i = 1, rig.partCount do
		local revealDist = rig.revealDist[i]
		local value = 1
		if profile and revealDist ~= math.huge then
			local frac
			if i <= rig.mainSegs then
				frac = (revealDist + rig.segLen[i] * 0.5) * invMain
			else
				local slot = math.floor((i - rig.mainSegs - 1) / rig.forkSegs) + 1
				local startFrac = rig.forkStartFrac[slot] or 0
				local along = revealDist - (rig.forkStartReveal[slot] or 0) + rig.segLen[i] * 0.5
				local localFrac = math.clamp(along / math.max(rig.forkLen[slot] or 1, 1e-4), 0, 1)
				frac = startFrac + localFrac * (1 - startFrac)
			end
			value = math.max(GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(math.clamp(frac, 0, 1), profile, seed), 0)
		end
		if value ~= rig.taper[i] then
			rig.taper[i] = value
			rig.lastWrittenLen[i] = -1
		end
	end
end

-- Rebuild the GrowthSpeed reveal mask against the current _tipDist over the freshly
-- sorted reveal order. reversed = negative GrowthSpeed: the strike travels from the
-- far end back toward the source (a segment shows once its far-end distance from
-- maxReveal falls within tipDist). Returns the new reveal pointer.
local function rebuildRevealMask(rig, tipDist, reversed)
	local ptr = 0
	local maxReveal = rig.maxReveal or 0
	for k = 1, rig.partCount do
		local idx = rig.revealOrder[k]
		local rd = rig.revealDist[idx]
		local visible
		if reversed then
			visible = rd ~= math.huge and (rd + rig.segLen[idx]) >= (maxReveal - tipDist)
		else
			visible = rd <= tipDist
		end
		if visible then
			rig.writeCFs[idx] = rig.rollCFs[idx]
			ptr = k
		else
			rig.writeCFs[idx] = FAR_CFRAME
		end
	end
	return ptr
end

-- Shared CFrame flush: reveal mask (GrowthSpeed) + batch write. atEmit runs before
-- the model is parented, so it writes CFrames directly (BulkMoveTo requires
-- workspace ancestry).
function Rig.flushCFrames(pData, atEmit)
	local rig = pData._rig
	local useReveal = pData._lSpeed ~= 0
	if useReveal then
		pData._revealPtr = rebuildRevealMask(rig, pData._tipDist or 0, pData._growReversed)
	end
	local cfs = useReveal and rig.writeCFs or rig.rollCFs
	if atEmit then
		for i = 1, rig.partCount do rig.parts[i].CFrame = cfs[i] end
	else
		workspace:BulkMoveTo(rig.parts, cfs, Enum.BulkMoveMode.FireCFrameChanged)
	end
end

-- Pool acquire with defensive rig re-check: a foreign / externally-mutilated model
-- or a layout change that slipped past the _PoolGen flush rebuilds fresh.
function Rig.acquireBolt(data)
	local expected = Rig.layoutFor(data)
	if data.Pool ~= false then
		local model = Pool.acquire(data.RenderTemplate, "Lightning")
		if model then
			local rig = Rig.Rigs[model]
			if rig and rig.partCount == expected and rig.parts[1] and rig.parts[1].Parent == model then
				model:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
				return model, rig
			end
			pcall(function() model:Destroy() end)
		end
	end
	local model, rig = Rig.buildRig(data)
	model:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
	return model, rig
end

return Rig

--[[
	LinkCF  -  the one place LinkMode semantics are applied.
	Modes (read in GetData.luau): Follow / Pivot inherit the link POSITION only; Weld /
	WeldWithoutRotation inherit the full frame; RigidLocal inherits the frame snapshotted at emit
	(pData._rigidLocalParentCF) and ignores live link motion. Follow and Pivot differ only at spawn:
	Follow drops the link rotation, Pivot composes it (spawnFrame).
	Every emit / update / replay / bounce / preview site composes through these helpers; no other
	file branches on the mode strings (LinkService keeps its own reduced Weld/Follow set).
	Per-axis inheritance (item attrs LinkPosX..Z / LinkRotX..Z, absent = on): a masked axis never takes
	the link's value. For a user link it keeps the emitter's own position / rotation from spawn onward; a
	nested link masks against the link frame captured at emit. Rotation splits on a fixed YXZ order.
]]

local Constants = require(script.Parent.PartConstants)
local Pool = require(script.Parent.Pool)

local LinkCF = {}

-- Link frame with the nested parent-node offset applied (NestedEmit sets pData/emitCtx._linkLocal).
local function linkFrame(link, linkLocal)
	local cf = Constants.resolveLinkCFrame(link)
	if linkLocal then return cf * linkLocal end
	return cf
end

local LINK_AXIS_ATTRS = { "LinkPosX", "LinkPosY", "LinkPosZ", "LinkRotX", "LinkRotY", "LinkRotZ" }

-- Per-axis masks from the item; nil when every axis inherits (the common case, no per-frame cost).
function LinkCF.readAxes(item)
	local axes = nil
	for _, name in ipairs(LINK_AXIS_ATTRS) do
		local on = item:GetAttribute(name) ~= false
		if not on then axes = axes or {} end
		if axes then axes[name] = on end
	end
	if axes then
		for _, name in ipairs(LINK_AXIS_ATTRS) do
			if axes[name] == nil then axes[name] = true end
		end
	end
	return axes
end

-- Masked axes take the reference frame; enabled axes follow the live link.
local function maskFrame(liveCF, refCF, axes)
	local livePos, emitPos = liveCF.Position, refCF.Position
	local pos = Vector3.new(
		axes.LinkPosX and livePos.X or emitPos.X,
		axes.LinkPosY and livePos.Y or emitPos.Y,
		axes.LinkPosZ and livePos.Z or emitPos.Z)
	local rot = liveCF.Rotation
	if not (axes.LinkRotX and axes.LinkRotY and axes.LinkRotZ) then
		local lx, ly, lz = liveCF:ToEulerAnglesYXZ()
		local ex, ey, ez = refCF:ToEulerAnglesYXZ()
		rot = CFrame.fromEulerAnglesYXZ(axes.LinkRotX and lx or ex, axes.LinkRotY and ly or ey, axes.LinkRotZ and lz or ez)
	end
	return CFrame.new(pos) * rot
end

-- Reference frame for masked axes: the emitter's own frame for a user link, the link frame at emit
-- for a nested link (the source template's frame means nothing at the clone).
local function maskReference(pData, linkCF)
	local source = pData._sourceItem
	if pData._nestedDriven or not source or not source.Parent then return linkCF end
	return Constants.resolveLinkCFrame(source)
end

-- Emit-time reference for masked particles (RegisterEmit, after _nestedDriven). worldFrame captures lazily on replay.
function LinkCF.captureEmitFrame(pData)
	if pData.LinkAxes and pData.Link then
		pData._linkMaskRefCF = maskReference(pData, linkFrame(pData.Link, pData._linkLocal))
	end
end

-- Masks for the spawn-time helpers: user links only (nested links mask per frame against their emit frame).
function LinkCF.spawnAxes(data, emitCtx)
	if emitCtx and emitCtx._parentAlive ~= nil then return nil end
	return data.LinkAxes
end

-- Link frame with the spawn masks applied against the emitter's own frame.
local function maskedLinkFrame(link, linkLocal, axes, refCF)
	local frame = linkFrame(link, linkLocal)
	if axes and refCF then return maskFrame(frame, refCF, axes) end
	return frame
end

-- Follow / Pivot inherit position only; the Weld family inherits the full frame.
function LinkCF.positionOnly(mode)
	return mode == "Follow" or mode == "Pivot"
end

-- Motion is expressed in link space (VectorToObjectSpace) for the Weld family only.
function LinkCF.usesLinkSpace(mode, link)
	return (mode == "Weld" or mode == "WeldWithoutRotation" or mode == "RigidLocal") and link ~= nil
end

-- Reduce a link frame to what the mode inherits.
function LinkCF.applyPositionRule(mode, frame)
	if LinkCF.positionOnly(mode) then return CFrame.new(frame.Position) end
	return frame
end

-- Spawn frame under a link: Follow keeps the emitter's own rotation; a self-link IS the emitter
-- frame (composing both would apply its rotation twice); otherwise link rotation composes with the
-- emitter's rotation RELATIVE to its source parent (sourceParentCF, nested) or its world rotation.
-- Mirrored by MotionPreview so the preview matches the live spawn.
function LinkCF.spawnFrame(mode, link, emitter, sourceCF, linkLocal, sourceParentCF, axes)
	local linkCF = linkFrame(link, linkLocal)
	local frame
	if mode == "Follow" then
		frame = CFrame.new(linkCF.Position) * sourceCF.Rotation
	elseif link == emitter then
		frame = sourceCF
	else
		local relRot = sourceParentCF and (sourceParentCF.Rotation:Inverse() * sourceCF.Rotation) or sourceCF.Rotation
		frame = CFrame.new(linkCF.Position) * linkCF.Rotation * relRot
	end
	-- Masked axes spawn at the emitter's own pose (spawnAxes is nil for nested links).
	if axes then return maskFrame(frame, sourceCF, axes) end
	return frame
end

-- Origin frame for an emitter whose START rides a user link and is re-read through its life
-- (Lightning/Endpoints, every roll). Follow takes the link's position and keeps the emitter's own
-- rotation; Weld adds the link's rotation; Pivot takes that rotation once, at the first read;
-- RigidLocal stays where the link was at the first read. WeldWithoutRotation has no offset to
-- rotate here and reads as Follow. A link that is gone holds the last frame (nil if never read).
function LinkCF.originFrame(pData, link, emitter, sourceCF)
	local mode = pData.LinkMode
	if mode == "WeldWithoutRotation" then mode = "Follow" end
	if mode == "RigidLocal" and pData._originLinkCF then return pData._originLinkCF end
	if not link or link.Parent == nil then return pData._originLinkCF end
	local frame
	if mode == "Pivot" and pData._originPivotRot then
		local followed = LinkCF.spawnFrame("Follow", link, emitter, sourceCF, nil, nil, pData.LinkAxes)
		frame = CFrame.new(followed.Position) * pData._originPivotRot
	else
		frame = LinkCF.spawnFrame(mode, link, emitter, sourceCF, nil, nil, pData.LinkAxes)
		if mode == "Pivot" then pData._originPivotRot = frame.Rotation end
	end
	pData._originLinkCF = frame
	return frame
end

-- Parent frame from a LIVE link at emit time (no snapshot exists yet). Identity without a link.
function LinkCF.emitParentFrame(mode, link, linkLocal, axes, refCF)
	if not link then return CFrame.new() end
	return LinkCF.applyPositionRule(mode, maskedLinkFrame(link, linkLocal, axes, refCF))
end

-- Attachment visuals compose in their parent's space: a BasePart's CFrame, or an Attachment's
-- WorldCFrame (Animate visuals live under the source Attachment). Anything else is world space.
function LinkCF.toParentSpace(worldCF, visualParent)
	local convCF = CFrame.new()
	if visualParent then
		if visualParent:IsA("BasePart") then
			convCF = visualParent.CFrame
		elseif visualParent:IsA("Attachment") then
			convCF = visualParent.WorldCFrame
		end
	end
	return convCF:ToObjectSpace(worldCF)
end

-- Attachment variant of emitParentFrame, in `visualParent`-local space.
function LinkCF.emitAttachmentParentFrame(mode, link, visualParent, linkLocal, axes, refCF)
	if not link then return CFrame.new() end
	return LinkCF.applyPositionRule(mode, LinkCF.toParentSpace(maskedLinkFrame(link, linkLocal, axes, refCF), visualParent))
end

-- RigidLocal snapshot taken at emit: the frame the particle stays welded to. nil for other modes.
function LinkCF.rigidSnapshot(mode, link, frame)
	if mode == "RigidLocal" and link then return frame end
	return nil
end

-- Attachment snapshots keep the WORLD link frame; per-frame readers convert to parent space.
function LinkCF.rigidWorldSnapshot(mode, link, linkLocal, axes, refCF)
	if mode == "RigidLocal" and link then return maskedLinkFrame(link, linkLocal, axes, refCF) end
	return nil
end

-- A link is live while it is parented and the pool has not recycled it since this particle
-- captured it (pData._linkGen, stamped by RegisterEmit).
function LinkCF.isValid(pData, link)
	if not link or link.Parent == nil then return false end
	return Pool.linkGen(link) == (pData._linkGen or 0)
end

-- Link lost: keep the last good frame so the particle carries on from where its parent died
-- instead of collapsing onto the world origin. Readers see the frozen frame through parentFrame.
function LinkCF.freeze(pData)
	pData._frozenLinkCF = pData._lastLinkCF or CFrame.new()
	pData.Link = nil
end

-- World frame of the link as this particle sees it: the emit snapshot for RigidLocal (never
-- freezes), the live link otherwise. Records the frame so freeze() can keep it.
function LinkCF.worldFrame(pData, link)
	if pData.LinkMode == "RigidLocal" then
		return pData._rigidLocalParentCF or CFrame.new()
	end
	local cf = linkFrame(link, pData._linkLocal)
	local axes = pData.LinkAxes
	if axes then
		if not pData._linkMaskRefCF then pData._linkMaskRefCF = maskReference(pData, cf) end
		cf = maskFrame(cf, pData._linkMaskRefCF, axes)
	end
	pData._lastLinkCF = cf
	return cf
end

-- Live, frozen or snapshot frame for the per-frame readers; nil when the particle never had a link.
local function currentFrame(pData)
	if pData.LinkMode == "RigidLocal" then return pData._rigidLocalParentCF end
	local link = pData.Link
	if link then
		if LinkCF.isValid(pData, link) then return LinkCF.worldFrame(pData, link) end
		LinkCF.freeze(pData)
	end
	return pData._frozenLinkCF
end

-- Per-frame parent frame for Part / Model. Returns (parentCF, useVOS); identity when there never was a link.
function LinkCF.parentFrame(pData)
	local worldCF = currentFrame(pData)
	if not worldCF then return CFrame.new(), false end
	if LinkCF.positionOnly(pData.LinkMode) then return CFrame.new(worldCF.Position), false end
	return worldCF, true
end

-- Per-frame parent frame for Attachment, in visual-parent-local space. Returns (parentCF, useVOS, hasLink).
function LinkCF.attachmentParentFrame(pData)
	local worldCF = currentFrame(pData)
	if not worldCF then return CFrame.new(), false, false end
	local visualParent = pData.VisualPart and pData.VisualPart.Parent
	if not visualParent then return CFrame.new(), false, false end
	local linkLocalCF = LinkCF.toParentSpace(worldCF, visualParent)
	if LinkCF.positionOnly(pData.LinkMode) then return CFrame.new(linkLocalCF.Position), false, true end
	return linkLocalCF, true, true
end

-- LinkTrack reapply for Part / Model: WeldWithoutRotation rotates only the offset and keeps the
-- particle's own rotation; Follow / Pivot translate; Weld composes fully. Attachments have no
-- WeldWithoutRotation variant (LinkTrack applies applyPositionRule to them).
function LinkCF.reapplyFrame(mode, linkCF, localCF)
	if mode == "WeldWithoutRotation" then
		local worldOffset = linkCF:VectorToWorldSpace(localCF.Position)
		local rotOnly = localCF - localCF.Position
		return CFrame.new(linkCF.Position + worldOffset) * rotOnly
	end
	if LinkCF.positionOnly(mode) then return CFrame.new(linkCF.Position) * localCF end
	return linkCF * localCF
end

return LinkCF

--[[
	LinkService  -  standalone CFrame-tracking service.
	Users link arbitrary BaseParts / Models / Attachments to any target Instance
	(BasePart / Model / Attachment / Bone / Camera) using the same LinkMode dispatch
	as the particle runtime, without spawning particles.

	API:
	  LinkService:Activate()
	  LinkService:Deactivate()
	  LinkService:Link(part1, target, mode, duration)
	  LinkService:Clear(part1)
	  LinkService:IsLinked(part1) -> boolean

	mode: "Weld" | "Follow" | "Pivot" | "WeldWithoutRotation" (unknown -> "Weld")
	duration: optional number of seconds; nil = infinite. Entry auto-clears on expiry,
	          target destruction, or part1 destruction.

	Anchored is snapshotted at :Link time and forced true so Roblox physics does not
	fight per-frame CFrame writes; restored on :Clear / auto-expire.
]]

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local Constants = require(script.Parent.PartConstants)
local Log = require(script.Parent.Log)

-- Resume in PreRender on client (after physics + attachment-transform propagation
-- complete; matches the Lifecycle.luau LOOP_YIELD_EVENT choice). Heartbeat on server
-- since PreRender is client-only.
local TICK_EVENT = RunService:IsClient() and RunService.PreRender or RunService.Heartbeat

local LinkService = {}

LinkService._active = false
LinkService._connection = nil
LinkService._links = {}
LinkService._anchorSnapshot = {}
LinkService._warnedNotActive = false

local VALID_MODES = {
	Weld = true,
	Follow = true,
	Pivot = true,
	WeldWithoutRotation = true,
}

local function _readPart1CF(part1)
	if part1:IsA("Model") then
		local ok, cf = pcall(part1.GetPivot, part1)
		if ok and cf then return cf end
		return CFrame.new()
	end
	if part1:IsA("Attachment") then return part1.WorldCFrame end
	return part1.CFrame
end

local function _classifyPart1(part1)
	if part1:IsA("Model") then return "Model" end
	if part1:IsA("Attachment") then return "Attachment" end
	return "Part"
end

-- Snapshot prior Anchored state + force true. Attachment has no Anchored  -  returns nil.
-- BasePart returns a bool. Model returns a table {[BasePart] = priorAnchored} so non-
-- PrimaryPart members do not free-fall under gravity while PivotTo drives PrimaryPart.
function LinkService:_captureAndAnchor(part1)
	if part1:IsA("BasePart") then
		local prior = part1.Anchored
		part1.Anchored = true
		return prior
	end
	if part1:IsA("Model") then
		local snapshot = {}
		for _, desc in ipairs(part1:GetDescendants()) do
			if desc:IsA("BasePart") then
				snapshot[desc] = desc.Anchored
				desc.Anchored = true
			end
		end
		return snapshot
	end
	return nil
end

function LinkService:_restoreAnchor(part1)
	local prior = self._anchorSnapshot[part1]
	self._anchorSnapshot[part1] = nil
	if prior == nil then return end
	if part1:IsA("BasePart") and part1.Parent then
		part1.Anchored = prior
		return
	end
	if part1:IsA("Model") and type(prior) == "table" then
		for desc, priorAnchored in pairs(prior) do
			if desc.Parent then desc.Anchored = priorAnchored end
		end
	end
end

-- Start the per-frame link-tracking loop. Idempotent.
function LinkService:Activate()
	if self._active then return end
	self._active = true
	self._connection = TICK_EVENT:Connect(function(dt)
		self:_tick(dt)
	end)
end

-- Stop tracking + clear every active link, restoring each part1's prior Anchored state.
function LinkService:Deactivate()
	if not self._active then return end
	self._active = false
	if self._connection then
		self._connection:Disconnect()
		self._connection = nil
	end
	for part1 in pairs(self._links) do
		self._links[part1] = nil
		self:_restoreAnchor(part1)
	end
end

-- Pin `part1`'s CFrame to follow `target` every frame using `mode` (Weld / Follow /
-- Pivot / WeldWithoutRotation). `duration` (optional seconds) auto-clears the link
-- when elapsed; nil = persist until Clear. Anchored is snapshotted+forced true so
-- physics does not fight the per-frame CFrame writes; restored on Clear.
function LinkService:Link(part1, target, mode, duration)
	if not part1 or not target then return end
	if part1 == target then return end
	if not (part1:IsA("BasePart") or part1:IsA("Model") or part1:IsA("Attachment")) then return end
	if not part1.Parent or not target.Parent then return end
	if not VALID_MODES[mode] then mode = "Weld" end
	if not self._active and not self._warnedNotActive then
		self._warnedNotActive = true
		Log.warn("[Part-Icles LinkService] Link called before Activate(); the link won't update until you call LinkService:Activate(). This warning fires once.")
	end

	local targetCF = Constants.resolveLinkCFrame(target)
	local part1CF = _readPart1CF(part1)

	-- Snapshot Anchored on first Link only; re-Link of same part1 keeps the original
	-- prior-state so a Clear after multiple Links restores the truly-authored value.
	if self._anchorSnapshot[part1] == nil and not self._links[part1] then
		self._anchorSnapshot[part1] = self:_captureAndAnchor(part1)
	else
		-- Re-arm anchor flag in case user toggled it between Link calls.
		self:_captureAndAnchor(part1)
	end

	self._links[part1] = {
		target = target,
		mode = mode,
		offsetCF = targetCF:ToObjectSpace(part1CF),
		rotation = part1CF.Rotation,
		expiresAt = duration and (os.clock() + duration) or nil,
		partKind = _classifyPart1(part1),
	}
end

-- Stop tracking `part1`; restore its prior Anchored state. No-op if not linked.
function LinkService:Clear(part1)
	if not self._links[part1] then return end
	self._links[part1] = nil
	self:_restoreAnchor(part1)
end

-- Returns true when `part1` has an active link entry.
function LinkService:IsLinked(part1)
	return self._links[part1] ~= nil
end

function LinkService:_tick(dt)
	local now = os.clock()
	for part1, entry in pairs(self._links) do
		if not part1.Parent or not entry.target.Parent then
			self:Clear(part1)
		elseif entry.expiresAt and now >= entry.expiresAt then
			self:Clear(part1)
		else
			local targetCF = Constants.resolveLinkCFrame(entry.target)
			local newCF
			if entry.mode == "Weld" then
				newCF = targetCF * entry.offsetCF
			else
				-- Follow / Pivot / WeldWithoutRotation: position tracks the linked offset,
				-- rotation stays at the authored snapshot. WWR's mesh-frame variant from
				-- the particle pipeline doesn't apply outside emit; v1 treats it as Follow.
				newCF = CFrame.new((targetCF * entry.offsetCF).Position) * entry.rotation
			end
			if entry.partKind == "Model" then
				pcall(function() part1:PivotTo(newCF) end)
			elseif entry.partKind == "Attachment" then
				local parent = part1.Parent
				if parent and parent:IsA("BasePart") then
					part1.CFrame = parent.CFrame:ToObjectSpace(newCF)
				end
			else
				part1.CFrame = newCF
			end
		end
	end
end

return LinkService

--[[
	LinkTrack Mixin  -  per-frame link transform reapply for Part / Model / Attachment.
	Runs every Heartbeat (outside the step gate) so linked particles track their link every frame.
	`pData._localWorldCF` is the link-relative composed CFrame stashed by UpdatePart/Model/Attachment.
	Attachment composes in actualParent-local space, mirroring getAttachmentLinkCF in Update.luau.
]]

local LinkCF = require(script.Parent.LinkCF)

return function(Particle)

-- Per-frame link-CFrame writer. Composes `pData._localWorldCF` against the live link
-- target and writes the result to `pData.VisualPart` so linked particles track their
-- link every Heartbeat. No-op when pData.Link is nil or destroyed.
function Particle:ReapplyLink(pData)
	local link = pData.Link
	if not link then return end
	-- Destroyed or pool-recycled link: freeze the last good frame (LinkCF) so per-step
	-- updates keep composing from where the parent died; nothing to reapply per frame.
	if not LinkCF.isValid(pData, link) then
		LinkCF.freeze(pData)
		return
	end
	local lcf = pData._localWorldCF
	if not lcf then return end
	if not pData.VisualPart or not pData.VisualPart.Parent then return end
	local t = pData.Type
	if t ~= "Part" and t ~= "Model" and t ~= "Attachment" then return end

	if t == "Attachment" then
		local visualParent = pData.VisualPart.Parent
		if not visualParent then return end
		-- Attachments compose in their parent's space and have no WeldWithoutRotation variant.
		local linkLocalCF = LinkCF.toParentSpace(LinkCF.worldFrame(pData, link), visualParent)
		pData.VisualPart.CFrame = LinkCF.applyPositionRule(pData.LinkMode, linkLocalCF) * lcf
		return
	end

	local newCF = LinkCF.reapplyFrame(pData.LinkMode, LinkCF.worldFrame(pData, link), lcf)

	if t == "Model" then
		pData.VisualPart:PivotTo(newCF)
	else
		pData.VisualPart.CFrame = newCF
	end
end

end

--[[
	Log  -  console output gate shared by the plugin and the Part runtime.

	Log.enabled (default true) gates Log.print / Log.warn; error() is never gated.
	Plugin: the Settings panel's "Console Output" toggle sets it (SettingsToggles.luau).
	Standalone module: `require(Part_Icles).Log.enabled = false` silences the runtime.
]]

local Log = {}

Log.enabled = true

function Log.print(...)
	if Log.enabled then print(...) end
end

function Log.warn(...)
	if Log.enabled then warn(...) end
end

return Log

--[[
	Matte Mixin  -  Emit + Update for Mattes: a transformed Part that draws nothing itself and
	turns the part-icles nested in it into windows onto one picture.

	Every shape has a layer of its own (Matte/Layer): a picture shown on a sheet where the
	shape is, so the world hides it and is covered by it as a Highlight's Occluded mode does.
	The sheet lies in the face of the shape's box that the camera sees most of (View.sheet):
	a flat mesh's own surface, the near side of any other. What a shape stands on cannot cut
	its picture, and each mesh is sorted against the world on its own.
	That is View Mode Tilted. In the other modes (View.MODES) every shape shares ONE layer:
	on a sheet tilted into a face of the box around all the shapes (Semi Tilt), or on one
	that faces the camera at the shapes' middle, in front of them all, or right at the
	camera, over everything. One ViewportFrame for the whole play, and shapes that overlap
	fade as one picture.

	What the RenderTemplate carries is fired from the source (NestedEmit) with the copy as
	its link, each where it stands in the RenderTemplate, and marked as the Matte's. A shape
	is whatever of it is a part: a mesh part-icle's copy (EmitPart: _matteFor, _matteJoin),
	the chunks of a debris burst, the segments of a bolt or a rope and the parts of a Model
	part-icle's copy (_matteCarry: one shape, and one layer, for the pieces of one emit).
	Such a part plays in the world as it does anywhere, hidden, and a Glass twin of it stands
	in the layer's ViewportFrame (Matte/Twins), where Glass shows the layer's field
	(Matte/Field: planes with the Matte's texture) and nothing else: a window onto a picture
	laid on the screen, not on the mesh. The picture is square, Texture Scale view heights
	tall, centred on the view and repeated to fill it.
	Glass shows the field only on faces that look at the camera, so a DoubleSided mesh gets a
	mirrored twin for its other side (Matte/Sides), along the axis Back Faces names.
	The shapes move, turn, resize and change their mesh (Mesh Frames) by their own settings;
	their own colour, transparency, textures and flipbooks are left out. What a ViewportFrame
	cannot draw plays in the world at the shape's place: the emitters, beams, trails and
	lights in a shape's copy, and the Attachment, Beam, Trail, light and Highlight part-icles
	nested in it (a Highlight lies over the picture). A lightning's strike disk is left out.
	An item in Animate mode plays its own RenderTemplate and is no shape.

	Over the play's Lifetime the Matte's Brightness (above 1 glows where the place has a
	BloomEffect), Transparency (fades the whole layer) and Color (tints the picture) are read.
	A Matte with stored frames (Matte/Field) and a Flipbook Mode other than None plays them
	as its picture on the frame clock of Modules/Part/Flipbook: OneShot once over the
	Lifetime, Loop and PingPong at the Framerate. A flipbook's Timeline graph is that clock's
	own time over the play (0 its start, 1 its end): flat holds a frame, steeper plays
	faster; the picture's flipbook and the mask's each have one.
	A Matte with a stored mask lays it in front of its shapes: where the mask's texture is
	opaque the shapes are cut away and the world shows. The mask has a still texture and a
	flipbook of its own, on the same clock, which is what dissolves a shape. Where the mask
	is half see-through its own colour shows, a rim round every hole: Edge Color tints it
	and Edge Brightness makes it that many times as bright as the picture (View.glow).
	The play is kept until its Lifetime is over and its last shape is gone; shapes still
	there when it is taken away go with it.
	Client or plugin only: without a camera and a gui container nothing is emitted.

	Mutates: its own copy of the RenderTemplate and its layers (both made here). A shape's
	part is a CLONE its own play made; hidden here, it is never pooled. Field.store, called
	here in the plugin alone, writes the LIVE item's stored field.
	Cross-file: Emit.luau calls _matteFor before it reads a copy's decals and _matteJoin
	before it parents the copy; Rocks/init, Lightning/init, Rope/init and EmitModel call
	_matteCarry once their play's parts exist and before they are parented;
	Lightning/ImpactDisk reads pData._matteCarried; NestedEmit.walk forwards emitCtx._matte to
	deeper leaves; Engine.luau calls _placeMattes at the END of its frame step, after every
	play has moved and the camera has its final frame (Matte/Place).
]]

local GraphMod = require(script.Parent.Graph)
local RangeMod = require(script.Parent.Range)
local Constants = require(script.Parent.PartConstants)
local Pool = require(script.Parent.Pool)
local NestedEmit = require(script.Parent.NestedEmit)
local ParticlesMod = require(script.Parent.Particles)
local FlipbookMod = require(script.Parent.Flipbook)
local Preload = require(script.Parent.Preload)
local GuiHost = require(script.Parent.GuiHost)
local Log = require(script.Parent.Log)
local Field = require(script.Field)
local Layer = require(script.Layer)
local LayerPool = require(script.LayerPool)
local Looks = require(script.Looks)
local Place = require(script.Place)
local Twins = require(script.Twins)
local View = require(script.View)

-- A play whose clock is held still is dropped after this long in real time.
local STALLED_PLAY_SECONDS = 180

-- Field.store writes a SurfaceAppearance's texture, which only the plugin may.
local IS_PLUGIN = pcall(function()
	return game:GetService("Selection"):Get()
end)

return function(Particle)

local warnedNoScreen = false
-- The Matte plays alive, for the pass at the end of the engine's step.
local playing = {}
-- First stored frame -> true once its set was asked of the engine; a set stored anew has new frames.
local preloaded = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

-- Matte discriminator; shared by init.luau Emit dispatch + Lifecycle EmitAnimate dispatch.
function Particle._isMatte(item)
	return item:IsA("BasePart") and item:GetAttribute("IsMatte") == true
end

-- Plugin only: keeps a Matte item's stored texture the one its config names, and its stored
-- frames those of its MatteFlipbooks folder. Mutates the LIVE item's MatteField child.
function Particle:SyncMatteField(item)
	local config = item:FindFirstChild("PartIcleProperties")
	if not config then
		return false
	end
	local stored = true
	local changed = false
	local texture = config:GetAttribute("Texture") or ""
	if not Field.inStep(item, texture) then
		stored = Field.store(item, texture)
		changed = true
	end
	local frames = Field.flipbookTextures(item)
	if not Field.framesInStep(item, frames) then
		stored = Field.storeFrames(item, frames) and stored
		changed = true
	end
	local mask = config:GetAttribute("MaskTexture") or ""
	if not Field.maskInStep(item, mask) then
		stored = Field.storeMask(item, mask) and stored
		changed = true
	end
	local maskFrames = Field.flipbookTextures(item, Field.MASK_FLIPBOOK)
	if not Field.maskFramesInStep(item, maskFrames) then
		stored = Field.storeMaskFrames(item, maskFrames) and stored
		changed = true
	end
	-- The layers and the copies kept for the item are of what was stored before.
	if changed then
		LayerPool.drop(item)
		Looks.drop(item)
	end
	return stored
end

-- Destroys the layers and textures kept for later plays. Engine's Deactivate calls it.
function Particle:_dropMatteLayers()
	LayerPool.flush()
	Looks.flush()
end

-- Called by EmitPart with its new copy (a CLONE), before it reads the copy's decals: the play
-- of the Matte that carries this emit, or nil. A shape shows the field, not a look of its own.
function Particle:_matteFor(emitCtx, visualPart)
	local matte = emitCtx and emitCtx._matte
	if not matte or matte._released then
		return nil
	end
	for _, child in ipairs(visualPart:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("Decal") or child:IsA("SurfaceAppearance") then
			child:Destroy()
		elseif child:IsA("SpecialMesh") then
			child.TextureId = ""
		end
	end
	if visualPart:IsA("MeshPart") then
		visualPart.TextureID = ""
	end
	return matte
end

-- Gives a record its layer (its own, or the one the play's records share) and its place in the play.
local function seat(matte, record)
	-- A layer a record of this play has left keeps its planes: the next record takes it.
	record.layer = matte._layer or table.remove(matte._spare) or LayerPool.take(matte._sourceItem, matte._host, matte._folder)
	record.sheet = record.layer.sheet
	Twins.settle(record, record.layer.viewport)
	table.insert(matte._shapes, record)
end

-- Called by EmitPart before it parents a shape's copy (a CLONE): hides it in the world, keeps
-- the mesh's own colour and transparency off it, and stands its Glass twin in a layer.
function Particle:_matteJoin(matte, pData)
	local visualPart = pData.VisualPart
	pData.SkipTransparency = true
	pData.SkipColor = true
	-- A hidden copy must not be handed to a later play of the mesh.
	pData._noPool = true
	Twins.hide(visualPart)
	seat(matte, Twins.single(visualPart, matte.BackFaces))
end

-- Called by the emit of a play made of several parts (a debris burst, a bolt, a rope, a Model's
-- copy; all CLONES the play owns), once they exist and before they are parented: when a Matte
-- carries the emit, hides them in the world and shows them together, as one shape. `parts` is
-- the play's own list, or nil for every part under its visual that draws; `axes` and `spine`
-- name the box around them (Twins.group). Returns whether a Matte took them.
function Particle:_matteCarry(emitCtx, pData, parts, axes, spine)
	local matte = emitCtx and emitCtx._matte
	if not matte or matte._released then
		return false
	end
	local holder = pData.VisualPart
	parts = parts or Twins.partsOf(holder)
	pData._noPool = true
	pData._matteCarried = true
	for _, part in ipairs(parts) do
		Twins.hide(part)
	end
	seat(matte, Twins.group(holder, parts, matte.BackFaces, axes, spine))
	return true
end

function Particle:UpdateMatte(pData, dt, currentTime)
	local copy = pData.VisualPart
	if not copy or not copy.Parent then return true end
	if pData._parentAlive and not pData._parentAlive[1] then return true end
	if currentTime - pData.StartTime > STALLED_PLAY_SECONDS then return true end

	local timescale = 1
	if pData._tsOverride ~= nil and currentTime < (pData._tsOverrideUntil or 0) then
		timescale = pData._tsOverride
	end
	local elapsed = pData._effectiveElapsed
	if not pData._timeFrozen then
		elapsed = math.clamp(elapsed + dt * timescale, 0, pData.LifeTime)
		pData._effectiveElapsed = elapsed
	end

	local followed = pData._followItem
	if followed and followed.Parent then
		copy.CFrame = followed.CFrame
	end
	return elapsed >= pData.LifeTime and #pData._shapes == 0
end

-- Called by Engine.luau at the end of its frame step: lays every Matte play's layers.
function Particle:_placeMattes()
	LayerPool.sweep()
	Looks.sweep()
	if #playing == 0 then
		return
	end
	local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera
	if not camera then
		return
	end
	Place.begin()
	for _, pData in ipairs(playing) do
		Place.frame(pData, camera)
	end
	Place.finish()
end

function Particle:EmitMatte(item, link, emitCtx)
	if not item or not item.Parent then return end
	local data = self:GetEmitData(item, emitCtx)
	if not data or not data.RenderTemplate then return end

	local host = GuiHost.resolveContainer()
	local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera
	if not host or not camera then
		if not warnedNoScreen then
			warnedNoScreen = true
			Log.warn("[Part-Icles] a Matte draws on a player's screen: emit it from a LocalScript. Nothing was emitted.")
		end
		return
	end
	if IS_PLUGIN then
		self:SyncMatteField(item)
	end

	local copy = Pool.acquireOrCopyBare(data.RenderTemplate, "Matte", false)
	copy.Archivable = false
	-- Silent until fired below: an emitter left Enabled would start on its own once parented.
	for _, descendant in ipairs(copy:GetDescendants()) do
		if descendant:IsA("ParticleEmitter") then
			descendant.Enabled = false
		end
	end
	local worldCFrame, tiedToSource = Constants.playOrigin(item.CFrame, emitCtx)
	copy.CFrame = worldCFrame
	copy.Parent = data.EmitParent or NestedEmit.resolveCloneParent(item, link, emitCtx) or self:GetFolder()

	local graphs = {
		Brightness = data.Brightness,
		Transparency = data.Transparency,
		Color = data.Color,
		EdgeBrightness = data.MaskEdgeBrightness,
		EdgeColor = data.MaskEdgeColor,
		-- nil for the plain ramp (GetDataRig.readMatte): the flipbook then runs on the play's own time.
		FlipbookTime = data.FlipbookTime,
		MaskFlipbookTime = data.MaskFlipbookTime,
	}
	local pData = {
		Type = "Matte",
		VisualPart = copy,
		Events = data.Events,
		StartTime = os.clock(),
		TotalKeyFrames = 1,
		CurrentStep = -1,
		LifeTime = math.max(RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.Lifetime), 0.001),
		PartLife = 0,
		Graphs = graphs,
		Seeds = {
			Brightness = GraphMod.GenerateSeed(graphs.Brightness),
			Transparency = GraphMod.GenerateSeed(graphs.Transparency),
			EdgeBrightness = GraphMod.GenerateSeed(graphs.EdgeBrightness),
			FlipbookTime = graphs.FlipbookTime and GraphMod.GenerateSeed(graphs.FlipbookTime),
			MaskFlipbookTime = graphs.MaskFlipbookTime and GraphMod.GenerateSeed(graphs.MaskFlipbookTime),
		},
		_effectiveElapsed = 0,
		TextureScale = data.TextureScale,
		BackFaces = data.BackFaces,
		ViewMode = data.ViewMode,
		_host = host,
		_folder = self:GetFolder(),
		-- The layer every shape shares, in any View Mode but Tilted; nil there.
		_layer = nil,
		_sheet = {},
		-- Semi Tilt: the box around the shapes, and the shape whose axes it takes.
		_group = {},
		_lead = nil,
		_shapes = {},
		-- Tilted: layers whose shape is gone, for the play's next shapes.
		_spare = {},
		_picture = nil,
		_flip = nil,
		_mask = nil,
		_maskFlip = nil,
		_followItem = tiedToSource and item or nil,
	}
	pData._sourceItem = item
	-- Pool off: nothing an earlier play kept is taken, and this play keeps nothing.
	local pooled = data.Pool ~= false
	if not pooled then
		LayerPool.drop(item)
		Looks.drop(item)
	end
	if data.ViewMode ~= View.MODES.Tilted then
		-- One kept from an earlier play of this item has its planes already.
		pData._layer = LayerPool.take(item, host, pData._folder)
		pData._sheet = pData._layer.sheet
	end

	-- The stored frames, when the Matte plays a flipbook; the planes take copies of them.
	local frames = data.FlipbookMode ~= "None" and Field.frames(item) or {}
	if #frames > 0 then
		pData._flip = FlipbookMod.layerState(nil, frames, data.FlipbookMode,
			RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.FlipbookFramerate), data.FlipbookStartRandom, data.FlipbookReverse)
		if not preloaded[frames[1]] then
			preloaded[frames[1]] = true
			Preload.ask(frames)
		end
	end
	-- Where a layer's picture comes from (Matte/Layer): bare planes, and the stored frame they wear.
	pData._picture = {
		owner = item,
		backing = Field.BACKING,
		needsLook = false,
		plane = function(index)
			return Field.bare(index, "Field")
		end,
		look = function(frame)
			return frames[frame] or Field.still(item)
		end,
	}

	-- The mask: its frames when it plays a flipbook, else its still texture; none of either, no mask.
	local maskFrames = data.MaskFlipbookMode ~= "None" and Field.maskFrames(item) or {}
	local maskStill = Field.maskStill(item)
	if #maskFrames > 0 then
		pData._maskFlip = FlipbookMod.layerState(nil, maskFrames, data.MaskFlipbookMode,
			RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.MaskFlipbookFramerate), data.MaskFlipbookStartRandom, data.MaskFlipbookReverse)
		if not preloaded[maskFrames[1]] then
			preloaded[maskFrames[1]] = true
			Preload.ask(maskFrames)
		end
	end
	if #maskFrames > 0 or maskStill then
		pData._mask = {
			distance = Place.MASK_NEAREST,
			scale = data.MaskScale,
			frame = 0,
			from = {
				owner = item,
				needsLook = true,
				plane = function(index)
					return Field.bare(index, "Mask")
				end,
				look = function(frame)
					return maskFrames[frame] or maskStill
				end,
			},
		}
	end

	pData._onReclaim = function()
		pData._released = true
		local listed = table.find(playing, pData)
		if listed then
			playing[listed] = playing[#playing]
			playing[#playing] = nil
		end
		-- The layers are kept for the item's next play (Matte/LayerPool), their twins taken
		-- out first, or destroyed when the Matte's Pool is off; the hidden parts the twins
		-- stood for are taken away here.
		local function done(layer)
			if pooled then
				LayerPool.give(item, layer)
			else
				Layer.destroy(layer)
			end
		end
		for _, record in ipairs(pData._shapes) do
			Twins.destroy(record)
			if not pData._layer then
				done(record.layer)
			end
			Pool.dropCloneMap(record.holder or record.source)
			Twins.dismiss(record)
		end
		if pData._layer then
			done(pData._layer)
		end
		for _, layer in ipairs(pData._spare) do
			done(layer)
		end
		if not pooled then
			Looks.drop(item)
		end
	end
	-- Riding an emitted parent copy: die with it (see UpdatePointLight).
	if emitCtx and emitCtx._parentAlive and not data.EmitParent then
		pData._parentAlive = emitCtx._parentAlive
	end
	Particle._seedTsOverride(pData, item)

	pData._nestedAlive = { true }
	self:_registerEmit(pData, emitCtx)
	table.insert(playing, pData)

	-- The copy's own emitters play in the world; the copy holds nothing transformed (Pool.copyBare).
	local alive = self:_makeAliveCheck()
	for _, descendant in ipairs(copy:GetDescendants()) do
		ParticlesMod.EnableEmitSingle(descendant, alive)
	end

	NestedEmit.walk(self, data.RenderTemplate, copy, pData._nestedAlive, emitCtx, nil, function(carriedItem, carriedCtx)
		carriedCtx._matte = pData
		NestedEmit.keepPlace(carriedItem, carriedCtx, data.RenderTemplate)
	end)
end

end

--[[
	Matte/Field  -  the picture a Matte's shapes show: planes whose vertex alpha is 0. A
	ViewportFrame draws nothing for such a mesh until a Glass part stands in front of it, which
	then shows it (measured in Studio, 2026-10-12; an ordinary part, however transparent, is
	not shown that way, and the plane itself must be at Transparency 0).

	PLANES are unit squares in their own XY plane, facing +Z, that differ in their texture
	coordinates alone: across itself each repeats the picture `span` times, or shows that
	share of it when span is under 1, always centred on the picture's middle. Matte/View
	picks one by the size the picture is asked at, so a small picture needs no crowd of
	planes and a large one no plane beyond a part's size.

	A game script may not write SurfaceAppearance.ColorMap (it needs the Plugin capability), so
	the texture is STORED: the plugin keeps a SurfaceAppearance in the Matte item's child
	MatteField, a Folder, and a play copies it onto its planes. A Matte without one shows bare
	planes in its Color. A flipbook's frames are stored the same way, as SurfaceAppearances
	named 1..N in MatteField's own child Frames; what the user edits is the item's folder
	MatteFlipbooks of numbered Decals, as a mesh's MeshFlipbooks.

	The MASK is a plane of the same kind that stands in FRONT of the shapes, textured in
	AlphaMode Transparency: where its texture is opaque the plane is drawn, which hides the
	shape behind it and, the plane's own alpha being 0, leaves the layer empty there, so the
	world shows; where its texture is see-through the plane is not drawn and the shape is
	(measured in Studio, 2026-10-12). Its still texture and frames are stored in MatteField's
	child Mask (Still, and 1..N); its frames are the item's folder MatteMaskFlipbooks.
	The texture lies over the plane's own colour (AlphaMode Overlay), which is BACKING: where
	the image is transparent a shape shows that, not the grey a Glass part draws with nothing
	behind it.

	  Field.NAME                        the stored child's name
	  Field.SPANS                       every plane's span, ascending; a plane is named by its place here
	  Field.plane(index) -> MeshPart or nil   the loaded plane (never parented); nil while it loads
	  Field.bare(index, name) -> MeshPart or nil   a new plane for a play, with no texture; nil while the plane loads
	  Field.still(item) -> SurfaceAppearance or nil   the stored still picture
	  Field.BACKING                     the colour of a plane that wears a texture
	  Field.frames(item) -> { SurfaceAppearance }   the stored frames, in order
	  Field.flipbookTextures(item) -> { string }    the texture ids of MatteFlipbooks, in order
	  Field.store(item, texture) -> boolean
	      plugin only. Puts `texture` into the item's stored child ("" removes it); false
	      when the engine refuses the texture.
	  Field.inStep(item, texture) -> boolean   plugin only: the stored child holds `texture`
	  Field.storeFrames(item, textures) -> boolean   plugin only: the stored frames become `textures`
	  Field.framesInStep(item, textures) -> boolean  plugin only
	  Field.maskStill(item), Field.maskFrames(item)          the stored mask
	  Field.storeMask / maskInStep / storeMaskFrames / maskFramesInStep   as for the picture

	The store functions mutate the LIVE item (its MatteField child); everything else works
	on copies.
]]

local AssetService = game:GetService("AssetService")

local Field = {}

Field.NAME = "MatteField"
-- The item's folder of numbered Decals: the frames as the user keeps them.
Field.FLIPBOOK = "MatteFlipbooks"
-- The item's folder of numbered Decals for the mask.
Field.MASK_FLIPBOOK = "MatteMaskFlipbooks"
-- MatteField's children that hold the stored frames and the stored mask.
local FRAMES = "Frames"
local MASK = "Mask"
local STILL = "Still"

local PLANES = {
	{ span = 1 / 16, mesh = "rbxassetid://109697954021705" },
	{ span = 1 / 8, mesh = "rbxassetid://105515425430393" },
	{ span = 1 / 4, mesh = "rbxassetid://133204333374156" },
	{ span = 1 / 2, mesh = "rbxassetid://110201460857748" },
	{ span = 1, mesh = "rbxassetid://95616810785060" },
	{ span = 4, mesh = "rbxassetid://72910309858637" },
	{ span = 16, mesh = "rbxassetid://74445454192363" },
	{ span = 64, mesh = "rbxassetid://92190435164571" },
}
-- A load that failed is tried again after this many seconds.
local RETRY_SECONDS = 5
-- What a textured plane shows where its image is transparent.
local BACKING = Color3.new(0, 0, 0)
Field.BACKING = BACKING

Field.SPANS = {}
for index, entry in ipairs(PLANES) do
	Field.SPANS[index] = entry.span
end

local function quiet(part)
	part.Anchored = true
	part.CanCollide = false
	part.CanQuery = false
	part.CanTouch = false
	part.CastShadow = false
	part.Massless = true
	part.Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic
	part.Color = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
end

local function load(entry)
	entry.loading = true
	task.spawn(function()
		local ok, loaded = pcall(function()
			return AssetService:CreateMeshPartAsync(Content.fromUri(entry.mesh))
		end)
		entry.loading = false
		if ok and loaded then
			quiet(loaded)
			entry.plane = loaded
		else
			entry.failedAt = os.clock()
		end
	end)
end

function Field.plane(index)
	local entry = PLANES[index]
	if not entry then
		return nil
	end
	if entry.plane then
		return entry.plane
	end
	if not entry.loading and not (entry.failedAt and os.clock() - entry.failedAt < RETRY_SECONDS) then
		load(entry)
	end
	return nil
end

-- The texture the plugin stored on a Matte item, or nil.
local function storedAppearance(item)
	local stored = item and item:FindFirstChild(Field.NAME)
	return stored and stored:FindFirstChildOfClass("SurfaceAppearance")
end

function Field.still(item)
	return storedAppearance(item)
end

function Field.bare(index, name)
	local template = Field.plane(index)
	if not template then
		return nil
	end
	local field = template:Clone()
	field.Name = name
	field.Archivable = false
	return field
end

-- Children named by a number, in that order.
local function numbered(holder, className)
	local found = {}
	for _, child in ipairs(holder:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA(className) and tonumber(child.Name) then
			table.insert(found, child)
		end
	end
	table.sort(found, function(first, second)
		return tonumber(first.Name) < tonumber(second.Name)
	end)
	return found
end

function Field.frames(item)
	local stored = item and item:FindFirstChild(Field.NAME)
	local holder = stored and stored:FindFirstChild(FRAMES)
	if not holder then
		return {}
	end
	return numbered(holder, "SurfaceAppearance")
end

-- The stored mask's holder, or nil.
local function maskHolder(item)
	local stored = item and item:FindFirstChild(Field.NAME)
	return stored and stored:FindFirstChild(MASK)
end

function Field.maskStill(item)
	local holder = maskHolder(item)
	return holder and holder:FindFirstChild(STILL)
end

function Field.maskFrames(item)
	local holder = maskHolder(item)
	if not holder then
		return {}
	end
	return numbered(holder, "SurfaceAppearance")
end

-- The texture ids of one of the item's folders of numbered Decals (MatteFlipbooks unless named).
function Field.flipbookTextures(item, folderName)
	local folder = item:FindFirstChild(folderName or Field.FLIPBOOK)
	local textures = {}
	if folder then
		for _, decal in ipairs(numbered(folder, "Decal")) do
			local texture = decal.Texture
			-- A bare id is a content id a Decal accepts and a SurfaceAppearance may not.
			if string.match(texture, "^%d+$") then
				texture = "rbxassetid://" .. texture
			end
			if texture ~= "" then
				table.insert(textures, texture)
			end
		end
	end
	return textures
end

local function sameTextures(frames, textures)
	if #frames ~= #textures then
		return false
	end
	for index, frame in ipairs(frames) do
		if frame.ColorMap ~= textures[index] then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

function Field.framesInStep(item, textures)
	return sameTextures(Field.frames(item), textures)
end

function Field.maskFramesInStep(item, textures)
	return sameTextures(Field.maskFrames(item), textures)
end

function Field.maskInStep(item, texture)
	local still = Field.maskStill(item)
	if texture == "" then
		return still == nil
	end
	return still ~= nil and still.ColorMap == texture
end

function Field.inStep(item, texture)
	local stored = item:FindFirstChild(Field.NAME)
	if stored and not stored:IsA("Folder") then
		return false
	end
	local appearance = stored and stored:FindFirstChildOfClass("SurfaceAppearance")
	if texture == "" then
		return appearance == nil
	end
	return appearance ~= nil and appearance.ColorMap == texture
end

-- The item's stored child as a Folder, made when `wanted`. A holder of another class is
-- replaced: under a MeshPart a SurfaceAppearance would dress it.
local function holderOf(item, wanted)
	local stored = item:FindFirstChild(Field.NAME)
	if stored and not stored:IsA("Folder") then
		stored:Destroy()
		stored = nil
	end
	if not stored and wanted then
		stored = Instance.new("Folder")
		stored.Name = Field.NAME
		stored.Parent = item
	end
	return stored
end

-- A stored child that holds nothing any more is removed.
local function tidy(stored)
	if stored and #stored:GetChildren() == 0 then
		stored:Destroy()
	end
end

-- A SurfaceAppearance showing `texture`, or nil when the engine refuses it. A mask's cuts by
-- its alpha; a picture's lies over the plane's backing.
local function appearanceOf(texture, existing, masks)
	local appearance = existing or Instance.new("SurfaceAppearance")
	appearance.AlphaMode = masks and Enum.AlphaMode.Transparency or Enum.AlphaMode.Overlay
	local ok = pcall(function()
		appearance.ColorMap = texture
	end)
	if not ok then
		return nil
	end
	return appearance
end

function Field.store(item, texture)
	local stored = holderOf(item, false)
	local existing = stored and stored:FindFirstChildOfClass("SurfaceAppearance")
	if texture == "" then
		if existing then
			existing:Destroy()
		end
		tidy(stored)
		return true
	end
	local appearance = appearanceOf(texture, existing)
	if not appearance then
		return false
	end
	appearance.Parent = holderOf(item, true)
	return true
end

function Field.storeFrames(item, textures)
	local stored = holderOf(item, false)
	local holder = stored and stored:FindFirstChild(FRAMES)
	if holder then
		holder:Destroy()
	end
	if #textures == 0 then
		tidy(stored)
		return true
	end
	holder = Instance.new("Folder")
	holder.Name = FRAMES
	for index, texture in ipairs(textures) do
		local appearance = appearanceOf(texture, nil)
		if not appearance then
			holder:Destroy()
			tidy(stored)
			return false
		end
		appearance.Name = tostring(index)
		appearance.Parent = holder
	end
	holder.Parent = holderOf(item, true)
	return true
end

-- The stored mask's holder as a Folder under the item's stored child, made when `wanted`.
local function maskHolderOf(item, wanted)
	local stored = holderOf(item, wanted)
	local holder = stored and stored:FindFirstChild(MASK)
	if not holder and wanted then
		holder = Instance.new("Folder")
		holder.Name = MASK
		holder.Parent = stored
	end
	return holder
end

-- A mask holder that holds nothing any more is removed, and the stored child after it.
local function tidyMask(item)
	local stored = holderOf(item, false)
	local holder = stored and stored:FindFirstChild(MASK)
	tidy(holder)
	tidy(stored)
end

function Field.storeMask(item, texture)
	local existing = Field.maskStill(item)
	if texture == "" then
		if existing then
			existing:Destroy()
		end
		tidyMask(item)
		return true
	end
	local appearance = appearanceOf(texture, existing, true)
	if not appearance then
		return false
	end
	appearance.Name = STILL
	appearance.Parent = maskHolderOf(item, true)
	return true
end

function Field.storeMaskFrames(item, textures)
	for _, frame in ipairs(Field.maskFrames(item)) do
		frame:Destroy()
	end
	local made = {}
	for index, texture in ipairs(textures) do
		local appearance = appearanceOf(texture, nil, true)
		if not appearance then
			for _, frame in ipairs(made) do
				frame:Destroy()
			end
			tidyMask(item)
			return false
		end
		appearance.Name = tostring(index)
		table.insert(made, appearance)
	end
	if #made > 0 then
		local holder = maskHolderOf(item, true)
		for _, frame in ipairs(made) do
			frame.Parent = holder
		end
	end
	tidyMask(item)
	return true
end

return Field

--[[
	Matte/Layer  -  one shape's picture: an invisible quad in the world, the shape's sheet
	(View.sheet: in a face of the shape's own box), a SurfaceGui on it holding a ViewportFrame
	that fills it, the ViewportFrame's own Camera at the game camera's eye, and the field: the
	planes that carry the texture (Matte/Field). The shape's Glass twins are parented into the
	ViewportFrame by Matte/Twins. The quad covers what the camera sees of the shape and no more.

	The SurfaceGui sits in a gui container (GuiHost: CoreGui for the plugin, PlayerGui in a
	game) with the quad as Adornee: a ViewportFrame in a SurfaceGui that is parented in
	Workspace draws nothing (measured in Studio, 2026-10-12).

	Planes are laid in sheets: the picture behind every shape and, when the Matte has one, the
	mask in front of them all. A sheet has ONE set of planes, whatever its flipbook's length:
	a plane shows a frame by the SurfaceAppearance it wears, and the frame is changed by
	changing that (Matte/Looks keeps the item's copies of every frame between planes).

	  Layer.new(host, folder) -> layer      { quad, gui, viewport, eye, sheet, picture, mask }; hidden until placed
	  Layer.rest(layer)                     hides it for a later shape to take; its planes are kept
	  Layer.place(layer, camera, sheet, reach, scale, spans, from, frame, mask, shrink)   every frame
	      sheet is what View.sheet filled, or nil: the layer is then not shown.
	      from is where a sheet's planes and textures come from: { owner (the Matte item),
	      plane(index) -> a new bare plane of that span, or nil while it loads,
	      look(frame) -> the stored appearance of that frame (0 is the still picture) or nil,
	      backing (the colour of a textured plane, or nil), needsLook (a frame without a
	      texture is not shown: what is shown stays) }.
	      mask is nil or { distance, scale, from, frame }: the sheet in front
	  Layer.look(layer, brightness, transparency, color, edgeColor) every frame; writes what changed
	      color tints the picture, edgeColor (nil without a mask) the mask: its texture's own
	      colour shows where it is half see-through, the rim round a dissolve's holes
	  Layer.destroy(layer)                  takes the twins in the ViewportFrame with it

	Glow: SurfaceGui.Brightness above 1 is what a BloomEffect in Lighting picks up.
]]

local Looks = require(script.Parent.Looks)
local View = require(script.Parent.View)

local Layer = {}

-- Planes side by side overlap by this share, so no line of bare glass shows between two.
local LAP = 1.0005
-- Where a sheet's planes wait while it shows nothing: out of every view.
local PARKED = CFrame.new(0, 1e7, 0)

-- fields: the sheet's planes, columns x rows of `plane` of View's spans, or nil while that
-- plane loads. wears: what each plane wears for the frame `shown` (false for a bare plane),
-- a copy of stored[place]. shown is nil while the planes show nothing.
local function newSheet()
	return {
		fields = nil,
		wears = {},
		stored = {},
		shown = nil,
		away = false,
		side = 0,
		color = nil,
		places = {},
		plane = nil,
		columns = 0,
		rows = 0,
	}
end

function Layer.new(host, folder)
	local quad = Instance.new("Part")
	quad.Name = "MatteLayer"
	quad.Archivable = false
	quad.Anchored = true
	quad.CanCollide = false
	quad.CanQuery = false
	quad.CanTouch = false
	quad.CastShadow = false
	quad.Transparency = 1
	-- Unlocked, a click on it in Studio's viewport would select it.
	quad.Locked = true
	quad.Parent = folder

	local gui = Instance.new("SurfaceGui")
	gui.Name = "PartIclesMatte"
	gui.Archivable = false
	gui.ResetOnSpawn = false
	gui.Face = Enum.NormalId.Back
	gui.LightInfluence = 0
	gui.ZIndexBehavior = Enum.ZIndexBehavior.Sibling
	gui.SizingMode = Enum.SurfaceGuiSizingMode.FixedSize
	gui.Adornee = quad
	-- Not shown before its first place: a new quad stands at the world's origin.
	gui.Enabled = false
	gui.Parent = host

	local viewport = Instance.new("ViewportFrame")
	viewport.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	viewport.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	viewport.Ambient = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
	viewport.LightColor = Color3.new(0, 0, 0)
	viewport.Parent = gui

	local eye = Instance.new("Camera")
	eye.Parent = viewport
	viewport.CurrentCamera = eye

	return {
		quad = quad,
		gui = gui,
		viewport = viewport,
		eye = eye,
		-- Where View lays it, kept with the layer: the size of its picture outlives a play.
		sheet = {},
		picture = newSheet(),
		mask = nil,
		canvasX = 0,
		canvasY = 0,
		shown = false,
		brightness = 1,
		transparency = 0,
	}
end

-- `count` new planes of one span, or nil while that plane loads.
local function build(index, count, plane)
	local fields = {}
	for _ = 1, count do
		local field = plane(index)
		if not field then
			break
		end
		table.insert(fields, field)
	end
	if #fields < count then
		for _, field in ipairs(fields) do
			field:Destroy()
		end
		return nil
	end
	return fields
end

-- Takes what the sheet's planes wear off them, for other planes of the item to wear.
local function undress(sheet, owner)
	for place, worn in pairs(sheet.wears) do
		if worn then
			Looks.give(owner, sheet.stored[place], worn)
		end
		sheet.wears[place] = nil
		sheet.stored[place] = nil
	end
	sheet.shown = nil
end

-- Puts `frame` on the sheet's planes. False when the sheet needs a texture and the frame has none.
local function dress(sheet, from, frame)
	local stored = from.look(frame)
	if not stored and from.needsLook then
		return false
	end
	for place, field in ipairs(sheet.fields) do
		local worn = sheet.wears[place]
		if not worn or sheet.stored[place] ~= stored then
			if worn then
				Looks.give(from.owner, sheet.stored[place], worn)
			end
			local look = stored and Looks.take(from.owner, stored) or false
			if look then
				if from.backing then
					field.Color = from.backing
				end
				look.Parent = field
			end
			sheet.wears[place] = look
			sheet.stored[place] = stored or nil
		end
	end
	sheet.shown = frame
	-- A copy taken from the item's others carries the tint of the plane it came off.
	sheet.color = nil
	return true
end

-- Lays one sheet for this frame of the game: its planes across the view at `distance`, wearing `frame`.
local function lay(sheet, viewport, cameraFrame, fieldOfView, aspect, distance, scale, spans, from, frame)
	local index, side, columns, rows = View.fit(fieldOfView, aspect, distance, scale, spans)
	if not sheet.fields or index ~= sheet.plane or columns ~= sheet.columns or rows ~= sheet.rows then
		-- Another layout: what is shown stays, where it stood in the view, until its plane is loaded.
		local fields = build(index, columns * rows, from.plane)
		if fields then
			if sheet.fields then
				undress(sheet, from.owner)
				for _, field in ipairs(sheet.fields) do
					field:Destroy()
				end
			end
			for _, field in ipairs(fields) do
				field.CFrame = PARKED
				field.Parent = viewport
			end
			sheet.fields = fields
			sheet.plane = index
			sheet.columns = columns
			sheet.rows = rows
			sheet.side = 0
		end
	end
	local fields = sheet.fields
	if not fields then
		return
	end

	local laidOut = index == sheet.plane and columns == sheet.columns and rows == sheet.rows
	if laidOut and sheet.shown ~= frame then
		dress(sheet, from, frame)
	end
	if sheet.shown == nil then
		return
	end

	local places = sheet.places
	if laidOut then
		if side ~= sheet.side then
			sheet.side = side
			local lap = (#fields > 1) and LAP or 1
			local planeSize = Vector3.new(side * lap, side * lap, View.THICKNESS)
			for _, field in ipairs(fields) do
				field.Size = planeSize
			end
		end
		for row = 1, rows do
			for column = 1, columns do
				places[(row - 1) * columns + column] = View.tile(distance, side, column, columns, row, rows)
			end
		end
	end
	for place, field in ipairs(fields) do
		local kept = places[place]
		if kept then
			field.CFrame = cameraFrame * kept
		end
	end
	sheet.away = false
end

-- shrink: how much smaller the layer's scene is drawn toward the eye (1 when not given):
-- its planes stand that much nearer, as its twins do (Matte/Twins.scene).
function Layer.place(layer, camera, sheet, reach, scale, spans, from, frame, mask, shrink)
	shrink = shrink or 1
	local size = camera.ViewportSize
	local visible = sheet ~= nil and size.Y >= 1 and size.X >= 1
	if visible ~= layer.shown then
		layer.shown = visible
		layer.gui.Enabled = visible
	end
	if not visible then
		return
	end
	local aspect = size.X / size.Y
	local fieldOfView = camera.FieldOfView
	local cameraFrame = camera.CFrame
	layer.eye.CFrame = sheet.eyeFrame
	layer.eye.FieldOfView = sheet.eyeFov
	layer.quad.Size = sheet.quadSize
	layer.quad.CFrame = sheet.quadFrame
	if sheet.canvasX ~= layer.canvasX or sheet.canvasY ~= layer.canvasY then
		layer.canvasX = sheet.canvasX
		layer.canvasY = sheet.canvasY
		layer.gui.CanvasSize = Vector2.new(sheet.canvasX, sheet.canvasY)
	end

	lay(layer.picture, layer.viewport, cameraFrame, fieldOfView, aspect, View.behind(reach) * shrink, scale, spans, from, frame)
	local cover = layer.mask
	if mask then
		if not cover then
			cover = newSheet()
			layer.mask = cover
		end
		lay(cover, layer.viewport, cameraFrame, fieldOfView, aspect, mask.distance * shrink, mask.scale, spans, mask.from, mask.frame)
	elseif cover and cover.fields and not cover.away then
		-- Kept from a play that had a mask (Matte/LayerPool): its planes leave the view.
		cover.away = true
		for _, field in ipairs(cover.fields) do
			field.CFrame = PARKED
		end
	end
end

function Layer.look(layer, brightness, transparency, color, edgeColor)
	if brightness ~= layer.brightness then
		layer.brightness = brightness
		layer.gui.Brightness = brightness
	end
	if transparency ~= layer.transparency then
		layer.transparency = transparency
		layer.viewport.ImageTransparency = transparency
	end
	local picture = layer.picture
	if picture.fields and picture.shown ~= nil and color ~= picture.color then
		picture.color = color
		-- A textured plane is tinted through what it wears; a bare one takes the colour.
		for place, field in ipairs(picture.fields) do
			local worn = picture.wears[place]
			if not worn then
				field.Color = color
			elseif worn.Color ~= color then
				worn.Color = color
			end
		end
	end
	local cover = layer.mask
	if edgeColor ~= nil and cover and cover.fields and cover.shown ~= nil and edgeColor ~= cover.color then
		cover.color = edgeColor
		for place in ipairs(cover.fields) do
			local worn = cover.wears[place]
			if worn and worn.Color ~= edgeColor then
				worn.Color = edgeColor
			end
		end
	end
end

function Layer.rest(layer)
	layer.shown = false
	layer.gui.Enabled = false
end

function Layer.destroy(layer)
	layer.gui:Destroy()
	layer.quad:Destroy()
end

return Layer

--[[
	LayerPool  -  a Matte's layers outlive its plays. A layer is a quad, a SurfaceGui, a
	ViewportFrame with its camera and the planes of its picture and mask, and it keeps the
	size of its picture. A play that ends hands its layers here, rested with their planes,
	and the next play of the same item takes them. View Mode Tilted has a layer a shape, so
	a few plays at once hold a couple of hundred.

	LayerPool.take(item, host, folder) -> layer   one kept for the item, or a new one
	LayerPool.give(item, layer)   rests the layer and keeps it. Its twins must be gone already.
	LayerPool.drop(item)          the item's picture or mask was stored anew: the layers kept
	                              for it hold planes of the old one
	LayerPool.sweep()             destroys the layers nobody took for KEEP seconds. Called
	                              every frame; does nothing while none is kept
	LayerPool.flush()             destroys them all (the runtime stops)
	LayerPool.kept() -> count

	The lists are held by the item, strongly: a list that went with a collected item would
	leave its layers in the gui for good. The sweep empties and forgets every list in time.
	Cross-file: Particle:SyncMatteField (Matte/init) must call drop wherever it stores a
	picture, a mask or their frames; a kept layer would go on showing the old ones.
]]

local Layer = require(script.Parent.Layer)

-- Seconds a rested layer is kept, and the most kept in all.
local KEEP = 20
local MOST = 256

local LayerPool = {}

-- item -> { { layer, at }, ... }, the one that has rested longest first.
local pools = {}
local total = 0
