function LayerPool.take(item, host, folder)
	local list = pools[item]
	while list and #list > 0 do
		local entry = table.remove(list)
		total -= 1
		if #list == 0 then
			pools[item] = nil
		end
		-- A layer whose gui or quad was taken away from outside is none any more.
		if entry.layer.gui.Parent and entry.layer.quad.Parent then
			return entry.layer
		end
		Layer.destroy(entry.layer)
	end
	return Layer.new(host, folder)
end

-- The list whose first layer has rested longest.
local function oldest()
	local found, since = nil, math.huge
	for item, list in pairs(pools) do
		if list[1] and list[1].at < since then
			found, since = item, list[1].at
		end
	end
	return found
end

function LayerPool.give(item, layer)
	Layer.rest(layer)
	local list = pools[item]
	if not list then
		list = {}
		pools[item] = list
	end
	table.insert(list, { layer = layer, at = os.clock() })
	total += 1
	while total > MOST do
		local longest = oldest()
		if not longest then
			break
		end
		local kept = pools[longest]
		Layer.destroy(table.remove(kept, 1).layer)
		total -= 1
		if #kept == 0 then
			pools[longest] = nil
		end
	end
end

function LayerPool.drop(item)
	local list = pools[item]
	if not list then
		return
	end
	pools[item] = nil
	for _, entry in ipairs(list) do
		Layer.destroy(entry.layer)
		total -= 1
	end
end

function LayerPool.sweep()
	if total == 0 then
		return
	end
	local now = os.clock()
	for item, list in pairs(pools) do
		while list[1] and now - list[1].at > KEEP do
			Layer.destroy(table.remove(list, 1).layer)
			total -= 1
		end
		if #list == 0 then
			pools[item] = nil
		end
	end
end

function LayerPool.flush()
	for item, list in pairs(pools) do
		for _, entry in ipairs(list) do
			Layer.destroy(entry.layer)
		end
		pools[item] = nil
	end
	total = 0
end

function LayerPool.kept()
	return total
end

return LayerPool

--[[
	Looks  -  what a Matte's planes wear. A plane shows a frame of the picture, or of the
	mask, by the SurfaceAppearance parented to it, and a layer has ONE plane a sheet whose
	appearance is changed with the frame (Matte/Layer). The appearances are copies of the
	ones the plugin stored on the item (Matte/Field), since a game script cannot write a
	ColorMap, and a copy can be on one plane at a time. A copy taken off a plane waits here,
	with no parent, for the next plane of the item that shows that frame, so an item has
	about as many copies of a frame as planes show it at once.

	Looks.take(item, stored) -> appearance   a copy of `stored`, with no parent
	Looks.give(item, stored, appearance)     takes it off its plane and keeps it
	Looks.drop(item)     the item's picture or mask was stored anew: its copies are of the old one
	Looks.sweep()        destroys the copies of items that took and gave none for KEEP seconds.
	                     Called every frame; does nothing while none is kept
	Looks.flush()        destroys them all (the runtime stops)
	Looks.kept() -> count

	The lists are held by the item, strongly, and emptied by the sweep in time.
	Cross-file: Particle:SyncMatteField (Matte/init) must call drop wherever it stores a
	picture, a mask or their frames, as it does for Matte/LayerPool.
]]

-- Seconds an item's copies are kept after its planes last changed what they wear.
local KEEP = 20
-- Copies of one stored appearance kept at most: about the planes of an item that show one frame at once.
local MOST_OF_ONE = 96

local Looks = {}

-- item -> { at, lists = { stored -> { appearance, ... } } }
local pools = {}
local total = 0

function Looks.take(item, stored)
	local pool = pools[item]
	if pool then
		pool.at = os.clock()
		local list = pool.lists[stored]
		local kept = list and table.remove(list)
		if kept then
			total -= 1
			return kept
		end
	end
	local appearance = stored:Clone()
	appearance.Archivable = false
	return appearance
end

function Looks.give(item, stored, appearance)
	appearance.Parent = nil
	local pool = pools[item]
	if not pool then
		pool = { at = 0, lists = {} }
		pools[item] = pool
	end
	pool.at = os.clock()
	local list = pool.lists[stored]
	if not list then
		list = {}
		pool.lists[stored] = list
	end
	if #list >= MOST_OF_ONE then
		appearance:Destroy()
		return
	end
	table.insert(list, appearance)
	total += 1
end

local function empty(pool)
	for _, list in pairs(pool.lists) do
		for _, appearance in ipairs(list) do
			appearance:Destroy()
			total -= 1
		end
	end
end

function Looks.drop(item)
	local pool = pools[item]
	if pool then
		pools[item] = nil
		empty(pool)
	end
end

function Looks.sweep()
	if total == 0 then
		return
	end
	local now = os.clock()
	for item, pool in pairs(pools) do
		if now - pool.at > KEEP then
			pools[item] = nil
			empty(pool)
		end
	end
end

function Looks.flush()
	for item, pool in pairs(pools) do
		pools[item] = nil
		empty(pool)
	end
	total = 0
end

function Looks.kept()
	return total
end

return Looks

--[[
	Matte/Place  -  sets a Matte play's layers for one frame.

	Every record of the play (Matte/Twins: one mesh, or the pieces of one emit) is followed
	first: its twins are set to their parts, and it answers with the box it is shown by.
	View Mode Tilted: every record's own layer, on a sheet in a face of that box
	(View.sheet), the picture behind the box and the mask in front of it. Any other mode:
	the one layer the records share, on a sheet tilted into a face of the box around them
	all (Semi Tilt) or facing the camera (View.sharedDepth). Then the look: the Matte's
	Brightness, Transparency and Color over its Lifetime, the flipbook frame of the picture
	and of the mask, and the mask's edge.

	  Place.frame(pData, camera)    the Matte play's records, layers and look, for this frame
	  Place.MASK_NEAREST            the nearest a mask stands to the camera, in studs

	Mutates: the play's layers and twins, and pData._shapes (a record whose part is gone
	leaves the list; its layer rests in pData._spare for the play's next record).
	Cross-file: Matte/init calls Place.frame from _placeMattes, which Engine.luau runs at the
	END of its frame step: a sheet is cut to where its part stands, so laid any earlier it
	is a frame behind a part that moves or grows fast.
]]

local GraphMod = require(script.Parent.Parent.Graph)
local FlipbookMod = require(script.Parent.Parent.Flipbook)
local Field = require(script.Parent.Field)
local Layer = require(script.Parent.Layer)
local Twins = require(script.Parent.Twins)
local View = require(script.Parent.View)

local Place = {}

-- Semi Tilt: the record whose axes the group's box takes is kept until another looks this much larger.
local LEAD_KEEPS = 1.2
-- The mask stands at this share of the way to its shape, never nearer than MASK_NEAREST studs.
-- Near the shape, because a layer's camera cuts away what is nearly level with the eye over its sheet.
local MASK_SHARE = 0.9
Place.MASK_NEAREST = 1

-- The layers laid in the pass that is running, and the share of a screen's pixels each may
-- hold, from the pass before: many layers at once are each drawn smaller (View.shareOf).
local laid = 0
local share = 1
-- A share goes down at once and up only after this many passes that would all allow more:
-- every change of it gives every layer a picture of another size.
local RAISE_AFTER = 120
local roomFor = 0

function Place.begin()
	laid = 0
end

function Place.finish()
	local wanted = View.shareOf(laid)
	if wanted < share then
		share = wanted
		roomFor = 0
	elseif wanted > share then
		roomFor += 1
		if roomFor >= RAISE_AFTER then
			share = wanted
			roomFor = 0
		end
	else
		roomFor = 0
	end
end

-- The share of a screen's pixels a layer may hold in the pass that is running.
function Place.share()
	return share
end

-- A record whose part is gone: its twins go, and its own layer waits for the play's next record.
local function leave(matte, record)
	Twins.destroy(record)
	if not matte._layer then
		Layer.rest(record.layer)
		table.insert(matte._spare, record.layer)
	end
end

-- Sets the one layer the records share for this frame: a sheet where the View Mode puts it,
-- the picture behind the farthest record, the mask in front of the nearest.
local function placeShared(pData, camera, shown, mask)
	local frame = camera.CFrame
	local size = camera.ViewportSize
	local aspect = size.X / math.max(size.Y, 1)
	local shapes = pData._shapes
	local total = 0
	local count = 0
	local reach = 0
	local nearest = math.huge
	-- The scene's scale is the one worked out in the pass before: twins and planes take the same.
	local shrink = pData._shrink or 1
	local first = pData._shrink == nil
	local sceneReach = View.sceneReach(camera.FieldOfView, aspect)
	Twins.scene(frame.Position, shrink)
	-- The record that looks largest, and how large the kept lead looks.
	local largest = nil
	local largestLooks = 0
	local leadLooks = 0
	for index = #shapes, 1, -1 do
		local record = shapes[index]
		if not Twins.alive(record) then
			leave(pData, record)
			shapes[index] = shapes[#shapes]
			shapes[#shapes] = nil
		else
			local shapeFrame, shapeSize = Twins.follow(record)
			if shapeFrame then
				local centre = shapeFrame.Position
				local along = View.along(frame, centre)
				local half = shapeSize.Magnitude * 0.5
				total += along
				count += 1
				reach = math.max(reach, along + half)
				nearest = math.min(nearest, along - half)
				local looks = half / math.max((centre - frame.Position).Magnitude, View.NEAREST)
				if looks > largestLooks then
					largest = record
					largestLooks = looks
				end
				if record == pData._lead then
					leadLooks = looks
				end
			end
		end
	end
	-- A play's first pass has no scale from a pass before: it is worked out now and the twins
	-- set by it, or its first frame would be laid as it stands, on other planes than every later one.
	if first and count > 0 then
		shrink = View.shrinkFor(reach, nearest, sceneReach)
		if shrink ~= 1 then
			Twins.scene(frame.Position, shrink)
			for _, record in ipairs(shapes) do
				Twins.follow(record)
			end
		end
	end
	local sheet = nil
	if count > 0 and pData.ViewMode == View.MODES.SemiTilt then
		local lead = pData._lead
		if leadLooks == 0 or largestLooks > leadLooks * LEAD_KEEPS then
			lead = largest
		end
		-- Nothing looks like anything (records of no size): any that shows gives the axes.
		if not lead or not lead.frame then
			for _, record in ipairs(shapes) do
				if record.frame then
					lead = record
					break
				end
			end
		end
		pData._lead = lead
		local group = pData._group
		View.groupStart(group, lead.frame)
		for _, record in ipairs(shapes) do
			if record.frame then
				View.groupAdd(group, record.frame, record.size)
			end
		end
		local groupFrame, groupSize = View.groupBox(group)
		sheet = View.sheet(pData._sheet, frame, camera.FieldOfView, aspect, size.Y, groupFrame, groupSize, share)
	elseif count > 0 then
		local depth = View.sharedDepth(pData.ViewMode, nearest, total / count)
		sheet = View.facing(pData._sheet, frame, camera.FieldOfView, aspect, size.Y, depth, share)
	end
	if sheet then
		laid += 1
	end
	if mask and count > 0 then
		mask.distance = math.max(nearest * MASK_SHARE, Place.MASK_NEAREST)
	end
	Layer.place(pData._layer, camera, sheet, reach, pData.TextureScale, Field.SPANS, pData._picture, shown, mask, shrink)
	if count > 0 then
		pData._shrink = View.shrinkFor(reach, nearest, sceneReach)
	end
end

-- A flipbook's own time: the play's, or where its Timeline puts it at this point of the play.
local function clockOf(pData, position, elapsed, graph, seed)
	if not graph then
		return elapsed
	end
	return math.max(GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(position, graph, seed), 0) * pData.LifeTime
end

function Place.frame(pData, camera)
	local elapsed = pData._effectiveElapsed
	local frame = camera.CFrame
	local size = camera.ViewportSize
	local aspect = size.X / math.max(size.Y, 1)
	local fieldOfView = camera.FieldOfView

	local position = math.clamp(elapsed / pData.LifeTime, 0, 1)
	local graphs = pData.Graphs
	local seeds = pData.Seeds
	local brightness = math.max(GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(position, graphs.Brightness, seeds.Brightness), 0)
	local transparency = math.clamp(GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(position, graphs.Transparency, seeds.Transparency), 0, 1)
	local color = GraphMod.QueryColorPointWithTime(position, graphs.Color)
	-- The mask's edge has a brightness of its own: the layer takes the brighter, the other is dimmed.
	local edgeColor = nil
	if pData._mask then
		local edge = math.max(GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(position, graphs.EdgeBrightness, seeds.EdgeBrightness), 0)
		local pictureTint, edgeTint
		brightness, pictureTint, edgeTint = View.glow(brightness, edge)
		if pictureTint < 1 then
			color = Color3.new(color.R * pictureTint, color.G * pictureTint, color.B * pictureTint)
		end
		local authored = GraphMod.QueryColorPointWithTime(position, graphs.EdgeColor)
		edgeColor = Color3.new(authored.R * edgeTint, authored.G * edgeTint, authored.B * edgeTint)
	end

	local flip = pData._flip
	local shown = flip and FlipbookMod.frameIndex(flip, clockOf(pData, position, elapsed, graphs.FlipbookTime, seeds.FlipbookTime), pData.LifeTime) or 0
	local mask = pData._mask
	if mask then
		local maskFlip = pData._maskFlip
		mask.frame = maskFlip and FlipbookMod.frameIndex(maskFlip, clockOf(pData, position, elapsed, graphs.MaskFlipbookTime, seeds.MaskFlipbookTime), pData.LifeTime) or 0
	end

	if pData._layer then
		placeShared(pData, camera, shown, mask)
		Layer.look(pData._layer, brightness, transparency, color, edgeColor)
		return
	end

	local shapes = pData._shapes
	local sceneReach = View.sceneReach(fieldOfView, aspect)
	for index = #shapes, 1, -1 do
		local record = shapes[index]
		if not Twins.alive(record) then
			leave(pData, record)
			shapes[index] = shapes[#shapes]
			shapes[#shapes] = nil
		else
			local shrink = record.shrink or 1
			local first = record.shrink == nil
			Twins.scene(frame.Position, shrink)
			local shapeFrame, shapeSize = Twins.follow(record)
			local sheet = nil
			local reach = 0
			if shapeFrame then
				local along = View.along(frame, shapeFrame.Position)
				local half = shapeSize.Magnitude * 0.5
				reach = along + half
				record.shrink = View.shrinkFor(reach, along - half, sceneReach)
				-- A record's first pass: its scale is worked out now and its twins set by it.
				if first and record.shrink ~= 1 then
					shrink = record.shrink
					Twins.scene(frame.Position, shrink)
					Twins.follow(record)
				end
				sheet = View.sheet(record.sheet, frame, fieldOfView, aspect, size.Y, shapeFrame, shapeSize, share)
				if mask then
					mask.distance = math.max((along - half) * MASK_SHARE, Place.MASK_NEAREST)
				end
			end
			if sheet then
				laid += 1
			end
			Layer.place(record.layer, camera, sheet, reach, pData.TextureScale, Field.SPANS, pData._picture, shown, mask, shrink)
			Layer.look(record.layer, brightness, transparency, color, edgeColor)
		end
	end
end

return Place

--[[
	Matte/Sides  -  the other side of a Matte's shape.

	A Glass part shows the field only on the faces that look at the camera: a DoubleSided
	mesh draws its back faces as ordinary faint glass, which shows nothing (measured in
	Studio, 2026-10-12). A part whose CFrame is a mirror image (determinant -1) is drawn
	with its faces turned inside out, so a twin of the shape mirrored along one of its own
	axes shows what the shape cannot. The twin is the shape's other side only where the mesh
	is the same on both sides of that axis (a ring, a tube, a dome, a flat blade); any other
	mesh shows its mirror image from behind.

	  Sides.CHOICES                    what a Matte's Back Faces may be
	  Sides.axis(choice, size) -> "X" | "Y" | "Z" | nil
	      Auto mirrors a flat shape along its thin axis and any other along X
	  Sides.wanted(part) -> boolean    a DoubleSided MeshPart
	  Sides.twin(shape, axis) -> twin, mirror
	      the mirrored twin of a shape's Glass twin (a CLONE without children, not parented)
	      and the frame that mirrors: the twin stands at the shape's frame times it

	Cross-file: Matte/Twins makes the mirrored twin beside a shape's own, keeps both on their
	part and destroys both.
]]

local Sides = {}

-- Repeated in TypeDataMatte.BACK_FACES (TypeRegistry has no requires) and in the panel's dropdown.
Sides.CHOICES = { "Auto", "Off", "X", "Y", "Z" }

local MIRRORS = {
	X = CFrame.new(0, 0, 0, -1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1),
	Y = CFrame.new(0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, -1, 0, 0, 0, 1),
	Z = CFrame.new(0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, -1),
}
-- A shape is flat when its thinnest side is at most this share of its longest.
local FLAT = 0.1

function Sides.axis(choice, size)
	if MIRRORS[choice] then
		return choice
	end
	if choice ~= "Auto" then
		return nil
	end
	local longest = math.max(size.X, size.Y, size.Z)
	local thinnest, axis = size.X, "X"
	if size.Y < thinnest then
		thinnest, axis = size.Y, "Y"
	end
	if size.Z < thinnest then
		thinnest, axis = size.Z, "Z"
	end
	if thinnest <= longest * FLAT then
		return axis
	end
	return "X"
end

function Sides.wanted(part)
	return part:IsA("MeshPart") and part.DoubleSided
end

function Sides.twin(shape, axis)
	local mirror = MIRRORS[axis]
	local twin = Instance.fromExisting(shape)
	twin.Name = "OtherSide"
	twin.Archivable = false
	twin.DoubleSided = false
	twin.CFrame = shape.CFrame * mirror
	return twin, mirror
end

return Sides

--[[
	Matte/Twins  -  what a Matte's layer shows of a part.

	A part a Matte carries plays in the world as it does anywhere, hidden, and a twin of it
	stands in a layer's ViewportFrame as Glass, where Glass shows the layer's field. So
	whatever moves, sizes or reshapes the part knows nothing of the Matte, and what a
	ViewportFrame cannot draw (emitters, beams, trails, lights, a Highlight) plays in the
	world at the shape's own place. The twins are set to their parts once a frame.

	Measured in Studio, 2026-10-13:
	  A part is hidden by LocalTransparencyModifier 1 on itself and on each of its Decals
	  (the part's own does not reach them). It still casts a shadow, so that is switched off.
	  A Highlight draws on a hidden part only when the part is Glass, so the hidden part is
	  made Glass: a Highlight nested in a shape lies over the Matte's picture.
	  As Glass in a ViewportFrame a Part of any shape, a wedge, a truss, a union and a
	  MeshPart show the field. A MeshPart with a TextureID shows nothing, and ApplyMesh
	  brings the texture along. A SpecialMesh shows the field as a Brick, Sphere, Cylinder
	  or Wedge; a FileMesh one shows nothing, so its twin is a MeshPart of the same mesh
	  (AssetService:CreateMeshPartAsync, once per mesh; nothing shows until it is there).

	  Twins.hide(part)                    hides a play's own copy in the world, as above
	  Twins.partsOf(holder) -> { BasePart }    the parts under a holder that draw something
	  Twins.single(source, backFaces) -> record
	      one mesh: its twin and, for a DoubleSided MeshPart, the mirrored twin that shows
	      its other side (Matte/Sides). record.shape is the twin, nil while its mesh loads.
	  Twins.group(holder, parts, backFaces, axes, spine) -> record
	      the pieces of one emit (a debris burst, a bolt, a rope, a Model's parts), shown
	      together. `axes` (Twins.AXES) names the box around them: World, Pivot (the holder
	      Model's own frame) or Spine (along the line from the first to the last piece that
	      shows among the first `spine` of them).
	  Twins.settle(record, viewport)      parents the twins there; later ones follow
	  Twins.follow(record) -> CFrame, Vector3
	      sets every twin to its part and gives the box the record is shown by, kept as
	      record.frame and record.size; nil while nothing of it shows. A piece that stands
	      Twins.FAR studs off is parked by its rig and counts for nothing.
	  Twins.alive(record) -> boolean      the part, or the holder, is still in the place
	  Twins.destroy(record)               the twins
	  Twins.dismiss(record)               the hidden part or holder itself

	Mutates: the hidden parts (copies a play owns, which are never pooled afterwards) and
	the twins (CLONES made here, without children).
	Cross-file: Matte/init makes the records (_matteJoin, _matteCarry) and Matte/Place
	follows them at the end of the engine's step, after every play has moved its parts.
]]

local AssetService = game:GetService("AssetService")
local Sides = require(script.Parent.Sides)
local View = require(script.Parent.View)

local Twins = {}

-- Written as plain strings where _matteCarry is called (Lightning/init, Rope/init, EmitModel).
Twins.AXES = { World = "World", Pivot = "Pivot", Spine = "Spine" }
-- A rig parks the pieces it is not showing a thousand million studs out.
Twins.FAR = 1e8
-- Glass at this transparency shows the field cleanly; lower mixes in the glass's own grey.
local SHAPE_TRANSPARENCY = 0.99
-- A mesh that failed to load is asked for again after this many seconds.
local RETRY_SECONDS = 5

-- The SpecialMesh shapes that show the field as Glass.
local SCALED = {
	[Enum.MeshType.Brick] = true,
	[Enum.MeshType.Sphere] = true,
	[Enum.MeshType.Cylinder] = true,
	[Enum.MeshType.Wedge] = true,
}

function Twins.hide(part)
	part.Material = Enum.Material.Glass
	part.LocalTransparencyModifier = 1
	part.CastShadow = false
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("Decal") then
			child.LocalTransparencyModifier = 1
		end
	end
end

function Twins.partsOf(holder)
	local parts = {}
	for _, descendant in ipairs(holder:GetDescendants()) do
		if descendant:IsA("BasePart") and descendant.Transparency < 1 then
			table.insert(parts, descendant)
		end
	end
	return parts
end

local function dress(twin)
	twin.Name = "Shape"
	twin.Archivable = false
	twin.Material = Enum.Material.Glass
	twin.Transparency = SHAPE_TRANSPARENCY
	twin.LocalTransparencyModifier = 0
	twin.CastShadow = false
	if twin:IsA("MeshPart") then
		twin.TextureID = ""
	end
end

-- Mesh id -> { part (a dressed MeshPart, never parented), loading, failedAt }.
local meshParts = {}

-- The MeshPart of a mesh, or nil while it loads.
local function meshPart(meshId)
	local entry = meshParts[meshId]
	if not entry then
		entry = { part = nil, loading = false, failedAt = nil }
		meshParts[meshId] = entry
	end
	if entry.part then
		return entry.part
	end
	if entry.loading or (entry.failedAt and os.clock() - entry.failedAt < RETRY_SECONDS) then
		return nil
	end
	entry.loading = true
	task.spawn(function()
		local ok, made = pcall(function()
			return AssetService:CreateMeshPartAsync(Content.fromUri(meshId))
		end)
		entry.loading = false
		if ok and made then
			made.Anchored = true
			made.CanCollide = false
			made.CanQuery = false
			made.CanTouch = false
			dress(made)
			entry.part = made
		else
			entry.failedAt = os.clock()
		end
	end)
	return nil
end

-- A layer's scene is its shapes drawn smaller toward the eye when they are far (Matte/Place,
-- View.shrinkFor): every point at `shrink` of its way from the eye, every size by `shrink`.
-- The picture on the screen is the same, and its planes stay small enough to be one each.
-- Set for the layer whose records are followed next.
local sceneEye = Vector3.zero
local sceneShrink = 1

function Twins.scene(eye, shrink)
	sceneEye = eye
	sceneShrink = shrink
end

-- Where a twin stands in the scene for its part at `frame`.
local function seated(frame)
	if sceneShrink == 1 then
		return frame
	end
	return frame + (frame.Position - sceneEye) * (sceneShrink - 1)
end

-- Whether the scene has changed for a unit since it was last written.
local function sceneMoved(unit)
	return unit.shrink ~= sceneShrink or (sceneShrink ~= 1 and unit.eye ~= sceneEye)
end

-- Gives a twin the mesh its part has now; ApplyMesh brings the part's texture along.
local function reshape(twin, source)
	pcall(function()
		twin:ApplyMesh(source)
	end)
	twin.TextureID = ""
end

local function followPlain(unit)
	local source = unit.source
	local moved = sceneMoved(unit)
	local frame = source.CFrame
	if frame ~= unit.frame or moved then
		unit.frame = frame
		local seat = seated(frame)
		unit.twin.CFrame = seat
		if unit.other then
			unit.other.CFrame = seat * unit.mirror
		end
	end
	local size = source.Size
	if size ~= unit.size or unit.shrink ~= sceneShrink then
		unit.size = size
		unit.box = size
		unit.twin.Size = size * sceneShrink
		if unit.other then
			unit.other.Size = size * sceneShrink
		end
	end
	unit.shrink = sceneShrink
	unit.eye = sceneEye
	if unit.watch then
		-- A mesh made in memory has no id: its own size tells it from another.
		local meshId = source.MeshId
		local meshSize = source.MeshSize
		if meshId ~= unit.meshId or meshSize ~= unit.meshSize then
			unit.meshId = meshId
			unit.meshSize = meshSize
			reshape(unit.twin, source)
			if unit.other then
				reshape(unit.other, source)
			end
		end
	end
	unit.live = math.abs(frame.X) < Twins.FAR
end

-- A Brick, Sphere, Cylinder or Wedge SpecialMesh: the twin has a copy of it, kept to its Scale.
local function followScaled(unit)
	followPlain(unit)
	local scale = unit.mesh.Scale
	if scale ~= unit.scale then
		unit.scale = scale
		unit.twinMesh.Scale = scale
	end
	unit.box = unit.size * scale
end

-- A FileMesh SpecialMesh: the twin is a MeshPart of the mesh the SpecialMesh names now, as
-- large as the SpecialMesh draws it (the mesh's own size times Scale), where it draws it.
local function followFile(unit)
	local mesh = unit.mesh
	local meshId = mesh.MeshId
	if meshId ~= unit.meshId then
		unit.meshId = meshId
		if unit.twin then
			unit.twin:Destroy()
			unit.twin = nil
		end
	end
	local twin = unit.twin
	if not twin then
		local template = meshId ~= "" and meshPart(meshId) or nil
		if not template then
			unit.live = false
			return
		end
		twin = Instance.fromExisting(template)
		unit.twin = twin
		unit.meshSize = template.MeshSize
		unit.frame = nil
		unit.size = nil
		twin.Parent = unit.viewport
	end
	local frame = unit.source.CFrame
	if unit.offset then
		frame = frame * unit.offset
	end
	if frame ~= unit.frame or sceneMoved(unit) then
		unit.frame = frame
		twin.CFrame = seated(frame)
	end
	local size = unit.meshSize * mesh.Scale
	if size ~= unit.size or unit.shrink ~= sceneShrink then
		unit.size = size
		unit.box = size
		twin.Size = size * sceneShrink
	end
	unit.shrink = sceneShrink
	unit.eye = sceneEye
	unit.live = math.abs(frame.X) < Twins.FAR
end

-- One part and what stands for it in a layer. `watch`: its mesh may change (Mesh Frames).
local function newUnit(source, backFaces, watch)
	local unit = {
		source = source,
		twin = nil,
		other = nil,
		mirror = nil,
		viewport = nil,
		frame = nil,
		size = nil,
		box = nil,
		live = false,
		watch = false,
		meshId = nil,
		mesh = nil,
		twinMesh = nil,
		scale = nil,
		meshSize = nil,
		offset = nil,
		follow = followPlain,
	}
	local mesh = not source:IsA("MeshPart") and source:FindFirstChildOfClass("SpecialMesh") or nil
	if mesh and mesh.MeshType == Enum.MeshType.FileMesh then
		unit.mesh = mesh
		unit.follow = followFile
		local offset = mesh.Offset
		if offset.Magnitude > 0 then
			unit.offset = CFrame.new(offset)
		end
		return unit
	end

	local twin = Instance.fromExisting(source)
	dress(twin)
	unit.twin = twin
	unit.frame = source.CFrame
	unit.size = source.Size
	unit.box = unit.size
	unit.live = math.abs(unit.frame.X) < Twins.FAR
	if mesh and SCALED[mesh.MeshType] then
		local twinMesh = Instance.fromExisting(mesh)
		twinMesh.TextureId = ""
		twinMesh.Parent = twin
		unit.mesh = mesh
		unit.twinMesh = twinMesh
		unit.scale = mesh.Scale
		unit.box = unit.size * unit.scale
		unit.follow = followScaled
	elseif source:IsA("MeshPart") then
		unit.watch = watch
		unit.meshId = source.MeshId
		unit.meshSize = source.MeshSize
		local axis = Sides.wanted(source) and Sides.axis(backFaces, source.Size)
		if axis then
			unit.other, unit.mirror = Sides.twin(twin, axis)
		end
	end
	return unit
end

function Twins.single(source, backFaces)
	local unit = newUnit(source, backFaces, true)
	return { source = source, unit = unit, shape = unit.twin, frame = nil, size = nil }
end

function Twins.group(holder, parts, backFaces, axes, spine)
	local units = table.create(#parts)
	for index, part in ipairs(parts) do
		units[index] = newUnit(part, backFaces, false)
	end
	return {
		holder = holder,
		units = units,
		axes = axes or Twins.AXES.World,
		spine = spine or #parts,
		box = {},
		frame = nil,
		size = nil,
	}
end

local function settleUnit(unit, viewport)
	unit.viewport = viewport
	if unit.twin then
		unit.twin.Parent = viewport
	end
	if unit.other then
		unit.other.Parent = viewport
	end
end

function Twins.settle(record, viewport)
	if record.unit then
		settleUnit(record.unit, viewport)
		return
	end
	for _, unit in ipairs(record.units) do
		settleUnit(unit, viewport)
	end
end

local function followGroup(record)
	local units = record.units
	local spine = record.spine
	local first = nil
	local last = nil
	local live = 0
	for index = 1, #units do
		local unit = units[index]
		unit.follow(unit)
		if unit.live then
			live += 1
			if index <= spine then
				first = first or unit
				last = unit
			end
		end
	end
	if live == 0 then
		record.frame = nil
		record.size = nil
		return nil
	end

	local box = record.box
	if record.axes == Twins.AXES.Pivot then
		View.groupStart(box, record.holder:GetPivot())
	elseif record.axes == Twins.AXES.Spine and first and last ~= first then
		View.groupAlong(box, first.frame.Position, last.frame.Position)
	else
		View.groupWorld(box)
	end
	for index = 1, #units do
		local unit = units[index]
		if unit.live then
			View.groupAdd(box, unit.frame, unit.box)
		end
	end
	record.frame, record.size = View.groupBox(box)
	return record.frame, record.size
end

function Twins.follow(record)
	if record.units then
		return followGroup(record)
	end
	local unit = record.unit
	unit.follow(unit)
	record.shape = unit.twin
	if not unit.live then
		record.frame = nil
		record.size = nil
		return nil
	end
	record.frame = unit.frame
	record.size = unit.box
	return unit.frame, unit.box
end

function Twins.alive(record)
	local held = record.holder or record.source
	return held.Parent ~= nil
end

local function destroyUnit(unit)
	if unit.twin then
		unit.twin:Destroy()
		unit.twin = nil
	end
	if unit.other then
		unit.other:Destroy()
		unit.other = nil
	end
	unit.live = false
end

function Twins.destroy(record)
	if record.unit then
		destroyUnit(record.unit)
		record.shape = nil
		return
	end
	for _, unit in ipairs(record.units) do
		destroyUnit(unit)
	end
end

function Twins.dismiss(record)
	local held = record.holder or record.source
	if held.Parent then
		held:Destroy()
	end
end

return Twins

--[[
	Matte/View  -  where a shape's layer stands for a camera. Maths only.

	A layer is a picture (a ViewportFrame) shown on a quad where its shape is: being a real
	surface there, the engine hides it behind whatever stands nearer and draws it over what
	stands farther. Inside the picture, the field (the texture) fills the camera's view from
	behind the shape.

	The field is laid from square planes (Matte/Field): each repeats the picture `span` times
	across itself, or shows that share of it when span is under 1. A picture `scale` view
	heights tall is laid with the plane that covers the view by itself; where that plane
	would outgrow a part, planes that hold fewer whole pictures are laid side by side.

	  View.along(cameraFrame, position) -> studs along the camera's view (negative behind it)
	  View.farthest(fieldOfView, aspect) -> the greatest distance a view-filling plane can
	      stand at: a part is at most MAX_PART studs wide
	  View.depth(wanted, fieldOfView, aspect) -> `wanted` held between NEAREST and that
	  View.quad(cameraFrame, fieldOfView, aspect, depth) -> CFrame, Vector3
	      the quad: its Back face looks at the camera
	  View.behind(reach) -> how far the field stands: behind `reach`, the farthest a shape
	      reaches along the view
	  View.fit(fieldOfView, aspect, distance, scale, spans) -> index, side, columns, rows
	      which plane of `spans` (ascending), how large, and how many side by side
	  View.tile(distance, side, column, columns, row, rows) -> CFrame
	      a plane's place in the camera's own frame; the middle one is centred on the view
	  View.sheet(out, cameraFrame, fieldOfView, aspect, screenHigh, shapeFrame, shapeSize) -> out or nil
	      the sheet one shape's layer is shown on. The engine hides a layer by its sheet's
	      distance, so the sheet lies in a face of the shape's own box: the face that looks
	      largest from the eye (kept until another looks a fifth larger). The whole shape is
	      behind that plane, so nothing the shape stands on or in front of can cut its
	      picture, and what stands in front of the plane hides it. A flat shape's sheet is its
	      own surface. The quad is the box's shadow on that plane, cast from the eye, cut to
	      what the camera sees.
	      The layer's camera stands at the game camera's EYE with a skewed frame that stands
	      for a camera hanging squarely over the quad's middle: a map that keeps every point
	      of the sheet's plane keeps the picture on it, so the picture lines up from any
	      direction, however low the eye is over the plane. The engine reads a camera's frame
	      by dotting an offset with each axis, and refuses a frame holding a number much over 1
	      (measured in Studio, 2026-10-13): the axes are scaled to length 1 at most.
	      With the eye inside the box the sheet faces the camera and fills the view where the
	      camera's line leaves the box. nil when the shape is out of the view. Fills and
	      returns `out`: face (0 facing, else the axis 1..3 with the side's sign), quadFrame,
	      quadSize, eyeFrame, eyeFov, canvasX, canvasY
	  View.MODES: a Matte's View Mode. Tilted gives every shape the sheet above; the others
	      put all the shapes on ONE sheet. Semi Tilt lays that sheet as View.sheet lays one
	      shape's, for the box around all the shapes along the axes of the one that looks
	      largest:
	  View.groupStart(group, leadFrame), View.groupAdd(group, shapeFrame, shapeSize),
	  View.groupBox(group) -> CFrame, Vector3
	      that box, grown one shape at a time in a table the caller keeps
	  View.groupWorld(group), View.groupAlong(group, from, to)
	      start the box along the world's axes, or with its Z along the line from one point
	      to another (the world's axes when the two are nearly one point): the box around the
	      pieces of one emit (Matte/Twins), which has no shape to take its axes from
	      The other three face the camera and fill its view:
	  View.sharedDepth(mode, nearest, middle) -> how far ahead that sheet stands: the shapes'
	      mean distance (Middle), the nearest any of them reaches (Front), or right at the
	      camera, over everything (On Top)
	  View.facing(out, cameraFrame, fieldOfView, aspect, screenHigh, depth) -> out
	      that sheet, with the game's own camera frame
	  View.glow(brightness, edge) -> layerBrightness, pictureTint, edgeTint
	      a layer has ONE brightness for all it shows. With the mask's edge `edge` times as
	      bright as the picture, the layer takes the brighter of the two and the other's
	      colour is multiplied by its tint, which makes up for the difference
]]

local View = {}

-- A Matte's View Mode, as stored; TypeDataMatte.VIEW_MODES and the panel's dropdown repeat these strings.
View.MODES = { Tilted = "Tilted", SemiTilt = "Semi Tilt", Middle = "Middle", Front = "Front", OnTop = "On Top" }

-- A layer never stands nearer to the camera than this.
View.NEAREST = 0.5
-- Where an On Top sheet stands: past the camera's own near plane, nearer than anything worth showing.
local ON_TOP = 1
-- The engine's limit on a part's size.
local MAX_PART = 2048
-- How thick the quad and a field plane are.
View.THICKNESS = 0.05
-- The field stands this far behind the farthest shape: by this share of its distance, and by
-- at least this many studs.
local FIELD_SHARE = 0.5
-- The picture's plane stands this far out at most in a layer's own scene (View.shrinkFor).
local SCENE_REACH = 300
-- A plane overshoots the view by up to the step between two spans; a scene's reach keeps
-- such a plane this share of a part's size, since the scale in use is a frame old.
local SPAN_STEP = 4
local SCENE_SLACK = 0.9
local FIELD_BEYOND = 40
-- Planes laid side by side, each way, at most.
local MOST_ACROSS = 5
local SMALLEST_SCALE = 1e-4
-- A face counts as seen while the eye stands at least this share of its distance over it.
local FLATTEST = 0.002
-- The face a sheet lies in is kept until another looks this much larger.
local KEEPS = 1.2
-- A layer's camera sees between these, in degrees.
local NARROWEST_VIEW = 1
local WIDEST_VIEW = 120
-- A sheet's quad is this much larger than the shape's shadow, and the view it is cut to this much wider.
local SHEET_MARGIN = 1.02
-- A layer's picture is at most this many pixels a side.
local MOST_PIXELS = 2048
-- A line shorter than this gives a group's box no direction.
local SHORTEST_LINE = 0.05
-- A line steeper than this is squared up against the world's X axis, not its Y.
local UPRIGHT = 0.9

-- A picture's sides come in steps, each 1.41 times the one before, and a picture is made
-- smaller only after it has been far too large for a while: a new size is a new picture for
-- the engine to set up, and a sheet cut to a moving shape would ask for one every frame.
local LEAST_SIDE = 32
local STEPS_A_DOUBLING = 2
local ROOMY = 2.2
local SHRINK_AFTER = 45
-- All the layers shown together hold about this many screens of pixels, and none less than
-- LEAST_SHARE of one.
local PIXEL_BUDGET = 3
local LEAST_SHARE = 0.125
-- Past MANY_LAYERS at once the layers share what that many hold at LEAST_SHARE, each drawn
-- smaller again, down to FEWEST_SHARE of a screen.
local MANY_LAYERS = 48
local FEWEST_SHARE = 1 / 32

-- The step a side that needs `pixels` takes: the first that holds them.
local function stepOf(pixels)
	local steps = math.ceil(math.log(math.max(pixels, LEAST_SIDE) / LEAST_SIDE, 2) * STEPS_A_DOUBLING - 1e-9)
	return math.min(math.floor(LEAST_SIDE * 2 ^ (steps / STEPS_A_DOUBLING) + 0.5), MOST_PIXELS)
end

-- The size of the picture of a sheet that needs wantedX by wantedY pixels and may hold `most`
-- in all. `out` keeps the steps it stands on (keptX, keptY): they grow at once and shrink late.
local function picture(out, wantedX, wantedY, most)
	local stepX = stepOf(wantedX)
	local stepY = stepOf(wantedY)
	local keptX = out.keptX
	local keptY = out.keptY
	if not keptX or keptX < stepX or keptY < stepY then
		keptX = math.max(keptX or 0, stepX)
		keptY = math.max(keptY or 0, stepY)
		out.roomy = 0
	elseif keptX * keptY > ROOMY * stepX * stepY then
		out.roomy = (out.roomy or 0) + 1
		if out.roomy > SHRINK_AFTER then
			keptX = stepX
			keptY = stepY
			out.roomy = 0
		end
	else
		out.roomy = 0
	end
	out.keptX = keptX
	out.keptY = keptY
	if keptX * keptY <= most then
		return keptX, keptY
	end
	local fit = math.sqrt(most / (keptX * keptY))
	return math.max(math.floor(keptX * fit), 1), math.max(math.floor(keptY * fit), 1)
end

-- The share of a screen's pixels each of `count` layers may hold, in steps so it changes seldom.
function View.shareOf(count)
	if count <= PIXEL_BUDGET then
		return 1
	end
	if count > MANY_LAYERS then
		local crowded = math.ceil(math.log(count / MANY_LAYERS, 2) * STEPS_A_DOUBLING - 1e-9)
		return math.max(LEAST_SHARE * 2 ^ (-crowded / STEPS_A_DOUBLING), FEWEST_SHARE)
	end
	local steps = math.ceil(math.log(count / PIXEL_BUDGET, 2) * STEPS_A_DOUBLING - 1e-9)
	return math.max(2 ^ (-steps / STEPS_A_DOUBLING), LEAST_SHARE)
end

local function heightAt(fieldOfView, distance)
	return 2 * distance * math.tan(math.rad(fieldOfView / 2))
end

-- Planes of `side` that cover `extent` with one centred: an odd count.
local function across(extent, side)
	if side >= extent - 1e-6 then
		return 1
	end
	return 1 + 2 * math.ceil((extent - side) / (2 * side) - 1e-6)
end

-- The plane that shows the picture once.
local function whole(spans)
	for index, span in ipairs(spans) do
		if span >= 1 then
			return index
		end
	end
	return #spans
end

function View.along(cameraFrame, position)
	return (position - cameraFrame.Position):Dot(cameraFrame.LookVector)
end

function View.farthest(fieldOfView, aspect)
	return MAX_PART / (heightAt(fieldOfView, 1) * math.max(aspect, 1))
end

function View.depth(wanted, fieldOfView, aspect)
	return math.clamp(wanted, View.NEAREST, View.farthest(fieldOfView, aspect))
end

function View.quad(cameraFrame, fieldOfView, aspect, depth)
	local height = heightAt(fieldOfView, depth)
	return cameraFrame * CFrame.new(0, 0, -depth), Vector3.new(height * aspect, height, View.THICKNESS)
end

-- How much smaller a layer's scene is drawn toward the eye (Matte/Twins.scene): not at all
-- while the picture's plane stands within the scene's reach (View.sceneReach; SCENE_REACH
-- when none is given), else so much that it stands there. A plane is as large as the view
-- at its distance and a part is 2048 studs at most: past a few hundred studs a picture needs
-- several planes side by side (measured: 5 by 5 at 900 studs with Texture Scale 2). Never so
-- much that the nearest shape comes nearer than a stud, where its mask must still stand in front of it.
function View.shrinkFor(reach, nearest, sceneReach)
	sceneReach = sceneReach or SCENE_REACH
	local behind = View.behind(reach)
	if behind <= sceneReach then
		return 1
	end
	local least = 1
	if nearest > 1 then
		least = 1 / nearest
	end
	return math.clamp(sceneReach / behind, least, 1)
end

-- How far out a scene's picture may stand for this camera: where one plane still lays a
-- picture that repeats across the view, whatever its Texture Scale; SCENE_REACH at most.
function View.sceneReach(fieldOfView, aspect)
	local fits = MAX_PART * SCENE_SLACK / (SPAN_STEP * heightAt(fieldOfView, 1) * math.max(aspect, 1))
	return math.min(SCENE_REACH, fits)
end

function View.behind(reach)
	local wanted = math.max(reach, View.NEAREST)
	return wanted + math.max(wanted * FIELD_SHARE, FIELD_BEYOND)
end

function View.fit(fieldOfView, aspect, distance, scale, spans)
	local high = heightAt(fieldOfView, distance)
	local wide = high * aspect
	local cover = math.max(wide, high)
	local picture = math.max(scale, SMALLEST_SCALE) * high

	local index = #spans
	for candidate, span in ipairs(spans) do
		if span * picture >= cover then
			index = candidate
			break
		end
	end
	local side = spans[index] * picture

	-- Too large for a part: planes that hold fewer whole pictures, laid side by side.
	while side > MAX_PART and index > 1 and spans[index - 1] >= 1 do
		index -= 1
		side = spans[index] * picture
	end
	side = math.min(side, MAX_PART)
	-- A share of the picture cannot be laid side by side: the whole one, as large as a part may be.
	if side < cover and spans[index] < 1 then
		index = whole(spans)
		side = math.min(spans[index] * picture, MAX_PART)
	end

	local columns = across(wide, side)
	local rows = across(high, side)
	-- Smaller than the planes can tile: laid as small as they can.
	if columns > MOST_ACROSS or rows > MOST_ACROSS then
		side = cover / MOST_ACROSS
		columns = across(wide, side)
		rows = across(high, side)
	end
	return index, side, columns, rows
end

function View.tile(distance, side, column, columns, row, rows)
	return CFrame.new((column - (columns + 1) / 2) * side, ((rows + 1) / 2 - row) * side, -distance)
end

-- The polygon being cut, and the one it is cut into: a rectangle cut four times has eight corners at most.
local cornersX = table.create(12, 0)
local cornersY = table.create(12, 0)
local cutX = table.create(12, 0)
local cutY = table.create(12, 0)

-- Keeps the part of the polygon where a * x + b * y + c is not negative; returns its corner count.
local function cut(count, a, b, c)
	if count == 0 then
		return 0
	end
	local kept = 0
	local lastX = cornersX[count]
	local lastY = cornersY[count]
	local lastSide = a * lastX + b * lastY + c
	for index = 1, count do
		local x = cornersX[index]
		local y = cornersY[index]
		local side = a * x + b * y + c
		if (side >= 0) ~= (lastSide >= 0) then
			local share = lastSide / (lastSide - side)
			kept += 1
			cutX[kept] = lastX + (x - lastX) * share
			cutY[kept] = lastY + (y - lastY) * share
		end
		if side >= 0 then
			kept += 1
			cutX[kept] = x
			cutY[kept] = y
		end
		lastX = x
		lastY = y
		lastSide = side
	end
	cornersX, cutX = cutX, cornersX
	cornersY, cutY = cutY, cornersY
	return kept
end

-- How large a box face looks from the eye (its solid angle, nearly), or nil when the eye is
-- not over it. `along` is the eye's place on the face's axis, the others its place across.
local function looks(along, half, acrossFirst, acrossSecond, area)
	local height = math.abs(along) - half
	if height <= 0 then
		return nil
	end
	local distance = math.sqrt(height * height + acrossFirst * acrossFirst + acrossSecond * acrossSecond)
	if height < distance * FLATTEST then
		return nil
	end
	return area * height / (distance * distance * distance)
end

-- The face of the box that looks largest from `offset` (the eye in the box's own space):
-- its axis (1..3) with the side's sign, or 0 with the eye inside the box. `kept` has an edge.
local function largestFace(offset, size, kept)
	local best = 0
	local bestScore = 0
	local scoreX = looks(offset.X, size.X / 2, offset.Y, offset.Z, size.Y * size.Z)
	local scoreY = looks(offset.Y, size.Y / 2, offset.Z, offset.X, size.Z * size.X)
	local scoreZ = looks(offset.Z, size.Z / 2, offset.X, offset.Y, size.X * size.Y)
	if scoreX then
		best = offset.X > 0 and 1 or -1
		bestScore = best == kept and scoreX * KEEPS or scoreX
	end
	if scoreY then
		local face = offset.Y > 0 and 2 or -2
		local score = face == kept and scoreY * KEEPS or scoreY
		if score > bestScore then
			best = face
			bestScore = score
		end
	end
	if scoreZ then
		local face = offset.Z > 0 and 3 or -3
		local score = face == kept and scoreZ * KEEPS or scoreZ
		if score > bestScore then
			best = face
		end
	end
	return best
end

local function groupReset(group, origin, axisX, axisY, axisZ)
	group.origin = origin
	group.axisX = axisX
	group.axisY = axisY
	group.axisZ = axisZ
	group.lowX = math.huge
	group.lowY = math.huge
	group.lowZ = math.huge
	group.highX = -math.huge
	group.highY = -math.huge
	group.highZ = -math.huge
end

function View.groupStart(group, leadFrame)
	groupReset(group, leadFrame.Position, leadFrame.XVector, leadFrame.YVector, leadFrame.ZVector)
end

function View.groupWorld(group)
	groupReset(group, Vector3.zero, Vector3.xAxis, Vector3.yAxis, Vector3.zAxis)
end

function View.groupAlong(group, from, to)
	local line = to - from
	local length = line.Magnitude
	if length < SHORTEST_LINE then
		View.groupWorld(group)
		return
	end
	local axisZ = line / length
	-- Squared up against whichever of the world's axes the line leans on least.
	local helper = math.abs(axisZ.Y) < UPRIGHT and Vector3.yAxis or Vector3.xAxis
	local axisX = helper:Cross(axisZ).Unit
	groupReset(group, from, axisX, axisZ:Cross(axisX), axisZ)
end

-- How far a box reaches to either side of its middle along a direction.
local function halfAlong(direction, frame, size)
	return (math.abs(direction:Dot(frame.XVector)) * size.X + math.abs(direction:Dot(frame.YVector)) * size.Y + math.abs(direction:Dot(frame.ZVector)) * size.Z) / 2
end

function View.groupAdd(group, shapeFrame, shapeSize)
	local offset = shapeFrame.Position - group.origin
	local middle = offset:Dot(group.axisX)
	local half = halfAlong(group.axisX, shapeFrame, shapeSize)
	group.lowX = math.min(group.lowX, middle - half)
	group.highX = math.max(group.highX, middle + half)
	middle = offset:Dot(group.axisY)
	half = halfAlong(group.axisY, shapeFrame, shapeSize)
	group.lowY = math.min(group.lowY, middle - half)
	group.highY = math.max(group.highY, middle + half)
	middle = offset:Dot(group.axisZ)
	half = halfAlong(group.axisZ, shapeFrame, shapeSize)
	group.lowZ = math.min(group.lowZ, middle - half)
	group.highZ = math.max(group.highZ, middle + half)
end

function View.groupBox(group)
	local centre = group.origin + group.axisX * ((group.lowX + group.highX) / 2) + group.axisY * ((group.lowY + group.highY) / 2) + group.axisZ * ((group.lowZ + group.highZ) / 2)
	return CFrame.fromMatrix(centre, group.axisX, group.axisY, group.axisZ), Vector3.new(group.highX - group.lowX, group.highY - group.lowY, group.highZ - group.lowZ)
end

-- An edge brighter than this many pictures would leave the picture too few shades to draw in.
local MOST_GLOW = 8
-- A tint of t dims a plane as a layer brightness of t ^ TINT_POWER would (measured in Studio,
-- 2026-10-13: within 3 in a hundred up to 8 times).
local TINT_POWER = 1.8

function View.glow(brightness, edge)
	local held = math.min(edge, MOST_GLOW)
	local most = math.max(held, 1)
	return brightness * most, (1 / most) ^ (1 / TINT_POWER), (held / most) ^ (1 / TINT_POWER)
end

function View.sharedDepth(mode, nearest, middle)
	if mode == View.MODES.OnTop then
		return ON_TOP
	elseif mode == View.MODES.Front then
		return nearest
	end
	return middle
end

-- share: the share of the screen's pixels the picture may hold (1 when not given).
function View.facing(out, cameraFrame, fieldOfView, aspect, screenHigh, depth, share)
	local quadFrame, quadSize = View.quad(cameraFrame, fieldOfView, aspect, View.depth(depth, fieldOfView, aspect))
	local scale = math.sqrt(share or 1)
	out.face = 0
	out.quadFrame = quadFrame
	out.quadSize = quadSize
	out.eyeFrame = cameraFrame
	out.eyeFov = fieldOfView
	out.canvasX = math.max(math.floor(screenHigh * aspect * scale), 1)
	out.canvasY = math.max(math.floor(screenHigh * scale), 1)
	return out
end

-- How far along the camera's line the eye, standing inside the box, leaves it.
local function leaves(offset, heading, size)
	local nearest = math.huge
	if math.abs(heading.X) > 1e-6 then
		nearest = math.min(nearest, (math.sign(heading.X) * size.X / 2 - offset.X) / heading.X)
	end
	if math.abs(heading.Y) > 1e-6 then
		nearest = math.min(nearest, (math.sign(heading.Y) * size.Y / 2 - offset.Y) / heading.Y)
	end
	if math.abs(heading.Z) > 1e-6 then
		nearest = math.min(nearest, (math.sign(heading.Z) * size.Z / 2 - offset.Z) / heading.Z)
	end
	return nearest
end

function View.sheet(out, cameraFrame, fieldOfView, aspect, screenHigh, shapeFrame, shapeSize, share)
	local eye = cameraFrame.Position
	local offset = shapeFrame:PointToObjectSpace(eye)
	local face = largestFace(offset, shapeSize, out.face)
	if face == 0 then
		local inside = math.abs(offset.X) <= shapeSize.X / 2 and math.abs(offset.Y) <= shapeSize.Y / 2 and math.abs(offset.Z) <= shapeSize.Z / 2
		local depth = View.along(cameraFrame, shapeFrame.Position)
		if inside then
			depth = leaves(offset, shapeFrame:VectorToObjectSpace(cameraFrame.LookVector), shapeSize)
		elseif depth < View.NEAREST then
			return nil
		end
		return View.facing(out, cameraFrame, fieldOfView, aspect, screenHigh, depth, share)
	end

	-- The face's frame: `toward` out of the box at the eye, `right` x `up` = `toward`; the
	-- face is 2 * halfWide by 2 * halfHigh, the box `deep` behind it, the eye at
	-- (eyeAcross, eyeUp) over it, `height` studs off.
	local axisX = shapeFrame.XVector
	local axisY = shapeFrame.YVector
	local axisZ = shapeFrame.ZVector
	local toward, right, up, halfWide, halfHigh, deep, eyeAcross, eyeUp, height
	if face == 1 or face == -1 then
		toward, right, up = axisX, axisY, axisZ
		halfWide, halfHigh, deep = shapeSize.Y / 2, shapeSize.Z / 2, shapeSize.X
		eyeAcross, eyeUp, height = offset.Y, offset.Z, math.abs(offset.X) - shapeSize.X / 2
	elseif face == 2 or face == -2 then
		toward, right, up = axisY, axisZ, axisX
		halfWide, halfHigh, deep = shapeSize.Z / 2, shapeSize.X / 2, shapeSize.Y
		eyeAcross, eyeUp, height = offset.Z, offset.X, math.abs(offset.Y) - shapeSize.Y / 2
	else
		toward, right, up = axisZ, axisX, axisY
		halfWide, halfHigh, deep = shapeSize.X / 2, shapeSize.Y / 2, shapeSize.Z
		eyeAcross, eyeUp, height = offset.X, offset.Y, math.abs(offset.Z) - shapeSize.Z / 2
	end
	-- The far side of an axis: the frame turned about `right` x `up`, still right-handed.
	if face < 0 then
		toward = -toward
		right, up = up, right
		halfWide, halfHigh = halfHigh, halfWide
		eyeAcross, eyeUp = eyeUp, eyeAcross
	end
	local faceCentre = shapeFrame.Position + toward * (deep / 2)

	-- The box's shadow on the face's plane: the face itself, and the far face drawn toward the eye's foot.
	local drawn = height / (height + deep)
	local left = math.min(-halfWide, eyeAcross + (-halfWide - eyeAcross) * drawn)
	local rightmost = math.max(halfWide, eyeAcross + (halfWide - eyeAcross) * drawn)
	local bottom = math.min(-halfHigh, eyeUp + (-halfHigh - eyeUp) * drawn)
	local top = math.max(halfHigh, eyeUp + (halfHigh - eyeUp) * drawn)
	local grow = (SHEET_MARGIN - 1) / 2
	local growAcross = (rightmost - left) * grow
	local growUp = (top - bottom) * grow
	cornersX[1], cornersY[1] = left - growAcross, bottom - growUp
	cornersX[2], cornersY[2] = rightmost + growAcross, bottom - growUp
	cornersX[3], cornersY[3] = rightmost + growAcross, top + growUp
	cornersX[4], cornersY[4] = left - growAcross, top + growUp

	-- Cut to the camera's view: each side of the view is a line on the plane.
	local look = cameraFrame.LookVector
	local tangentHigh = math.tan(math.rad(fieldOfView / 2)) * SHEET_MARGIN
	local tangentWide = tangentHigh * aspect
	local count = 4
	for side = 1, 4 do
		local inward
		if side == 1 then
			inward = look * tangentWide - cameraFrame.RightVector
		elseif side == 2 then
			inward = look * tangentWide + cameraFrame.RightVector
		elseif side == 3 then
			inward = look * tangentHigh - cameraFrame.UpVector
		else
			inward = look * tangentHigh + cameraFrame.UpVector
		end
		local a = inward:Dot(right)
		local b = inward:Dot(up)
		count = cut(count, a, b, -a * eyeAcross - b * eyeUp - height * inward:Dot(toward))
	end
	if count < 3 then
		return nil
	end
	left, rightmost, bottom, top = math.huge, -math.huge, math.huge, -math.huge
	for index = 1, count do
		left = math.min(left, cornersX[index])
		rightmost = math.max(rightmost, cornersX[index])
		bottom = math.min(bottom, cornersY[index])
		top = math.max(top, cornersY[index])
	end
	local wide = rightmost - left
	local high = top - bottom
	if wide < 1e-3 or high < 1e-3 then
		return nil
	end

	-- As many pixels a stud as the screen shows at the quad's nearest point, within what a
	-- picture may be and no more of them than its share of the screen.
	local aside = math.max(left - eyeAcross, eyeAcross - rightmost, 0)
	local above = math.max(bottom - eyeUp, eyeUp - top, 0)
	local nearest = math.sqrt(height * height + aside * aside + above * above)
	local most = screenHigh * screenHigh * aspect * (share or 1)
	local pixels = math.min(screenHigh / heightAt(fieldOfView, nearest), MOST_PIXELS / wide, MOST_PIXELS / high, math.sqrt(most / (wide * high)))
	-- The picture's size is one of a few steps, and the quad takes the picture's proportions:
	-- it grows about its middle to them, so the camera's picture still fills it exactly.
	local canvasX, canvasY = picture(out, wide * pixels, high * pixels, most)
	local density = math.min(canvasX / wide, canvasY / high)
	wide = canvasX / density
	high = canvasY / density

	-- The eye over the quad's middle, and the camera that stands for one hanging `hang` over it.
	local middleAcross = (left + rightmost) / 2
	local middleUp = (bottom + top) / 2
	local across = eyeAcross - middleAcross
	local upward = eyeUp - middleUp
	local reach = math.sqrt(height * height + across * across + upward * upward)
	local hang = math.clamp(reach, high / (2 * math.tan(math.rad(WIDEST_VIEW / 2))), high / (2 * math.tan(math.rad(NARROWEST_VIEW / 2))))
	local skewRight = right - toward * (across / height)
	local skewUp = up - toward * (upward / height)
	local skewBack = toward * (hang / height)
	local longest = math.max(skewRight.Magnitude, skewUp.Magnitude, skewBack.Magnitude)

	out.face = face
	out.eyeFrame = CFrame.fromMatrix(eye, skewRight / longest, skewUp / longest, skewBack / longest)
	out.eyeFov = 2 * math.deg(math.atan(high / (2 * hang)))
	-- The SurfaceGui is on the quad's Back face: that face lies in the plane.
	out.quadFrame = CFrame.fromMatrix(faceCentre + right * middleAcross + up * middleUp - toward * (View.THICKNESS / 2), right, up, toward)
	out.quadSize = Vector3.new(wide, high, View.THICKNESS)
	out.canvasX = canvasX
	out.canvasY = canvasY
	return out
end

return View

--[[
	MeshFrames  -  mesh sequence playback for Part visuals (a flipbook of MeshParts).

	A MeshFrames Folder under the item holds frames named 1..N: MeshParts, or Parts with a SpecialMesh.
	Each frame carries a mesh id and, optionally, a texture id. The visual steps through them on the
	particle's own clock (pData._effectiveElapsed, so Timescale / Pause / FreezeTime / reverse apply);
	the Size graph keeps driving the visual's size and every frame is fitted into that box.

	Two routes, chosen by the visual:
	  MeshPart          MeshPart:ApplyMesh with the frame instance (the only runtime-legal mesh change).
	                    ApplyMesh copies TextureID with the mesh, so a textured frame wins and an untextured
	                    frame gets the visual's current texture written back after the swap. The frame
	                    instances must exist in the place; the folder under the item guarantees that.
	  Part + SpecialMesh  SpecialMesh.MeshId and the frame's texture are written together: the texture goes
	                    to the RenderTemplate's first Decal / Texture (so a Neon part keeps glowing), else to
	                    SpecialMesh.TextureId. DecalLayers leaves that first decal's flipbook to this module.
	data.MeshFramesTextured (any frame with a texture) tells Emit to skip the legacy texture flipbook.

	Config attributes: MeshFrameMode ("None" / OneShot / Loop / PingPong), MeshFrameFramerate
	(NumberRange), MeshFrameStartRandom, MeshFrameReverse.

	Mutates the clone (Emit) or the LIVE RT (Animate: a backup of the mesh and texture taken at attach,
	restore() puts it back on finish and cancel). refresh() re-reads the settings per AnimateLoop cycle.
	The frame task allocates nothing per tick.
]]

local ContentProvider = game:GetService("ContentProvider")
local RangeMod = require(script.Parent.Range)
local MeshFlipMod = require(script.Parent.Flipbook)
local VisualHost = require(script.Parent.VisualHost)
local Log = require(script.Parent.Log)

local MeshFrames = {}

local MODES = { OneShot = true, Loop = true, PingPong = true }
local preloadedCount = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
local warnedUnsupported = false

-- Shared with the plugin's Mesh Frames panel and inventory insert so all three agree on what a frame is.
local function isFrame(inst)
	return inst:IsA("MeshPart") or (inst:IsA("BasePart") and inst:FindFirstChildOfClass("SpecialMesh") ~= nil)
end
MeshFrames.isFrame = isFrame

local function firstDecal(part)
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("Decal") or child:IsA("Texture") then return child end
	end
	return nil
end

-- Mesh id and texture id a frame carries ("" when untextured).
local function frameIds(frame)
	if frame:IsA("MeshPart") then return frame.MeshId, frame.TextureID end
	local mesh = frame:FindFirstChildOfClass("SpecialMesh")
	local decal = firstDecal(frame)
	local texture = (decal and decal.Texture ~= "" and decal.Texture) or mesh.TextureId
	return mesh.MeshId, texture
end

-- Frames under the folder sorted by numeric name; preloaded whenever the count changes.
function MeshFrames.readFrames(folder)
	local frames = {}
	if not folder then return frames end
	for _, child in ipairs(folder:GetChildren()) do
		if isFrame(child) then table.insert(frames, child) end
	end
	table.sort(frames, function(a, b)
		return (tonumber(a.Name) or 0) < (tonumber(b.Name) or 0)
	end)
	if #frames > 0 and preloadedCount[folder] ~= #frames then
		preloadedCount[folder] = #frames
		task.spawn(function()
			pcall(function() ContentProvider:PreloadAsync(frames) end)
		end)
	end
	return frames
end

-- GetData hook.
function MeshFrames.readInto(data, item, config)
	data.MeshFrames = MeshFrames.readFrames(item:FindFirstChild("MeshFrames"))
	data.MeshFrameMeshIds = {}
	data.MeshFrameTextures = {}
	data.MeshFramesTextured = false
	for index, frame in ipairs(data.MeshFrames) do
		local meshId, texture = frameIds(frame)
		data.MeshFrameMeshIds[index] = meshId
		data.MeshFrameTextures[index] = texture
		if texture ~= "" then data.MeshFramesTextured = true end
	end
	local mode = config:GetAttribute("MeshFrameMode")
	if typeof(mode) == "EnumItem" then mode = mode.Name end
	data.MeshFrameMode = MODES[mode] and mode or "None"
	data.MeshFrameFramerate = config:GetAttribute("MeshFrameFramerate") or NumberRange.new(24)
	data.MeshFrameStartRandom = config:GetAttribute("MeshFrameStartRandom") == true
	data.MeshFrameReverse = config:GetAttribute("MeshFrameReverse") == true
end

local function isActive(data)
	return data.MeshFrames ~= nil and #data.MeshFrames > 0 and data.MeshFrameMode ~= "None"
end

local function buildState(data, visualPart)
	local framerate = RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.MeshFrameFramerate)
	local state = MeshFlipMod.layerState(visualPart, data.MeshFrames, data.MeshFrameMode, framerate,
		data.MeshFrameStartRandom, data.MeshFrameReverse)
	state.meshIds = data.MeshFrameMeshIds
	state.textures = data.MeshFrameTextures
	return state
end

-- Where the SpecialMesh route writes the frame texture: the first decal, else the mesh itself.
local function textureSlot(visualPart, specialMesh)
	local decal = firstDecal(visualPart)
	if decal then return decal, "Texture" end
	return specialMesh, "TextureId"
end

local function applyFrame(state, visual, index)
	pcall(function()
		if state.specialMesh then
			state.specialMesh.MeshId = state.meshIds[index]
			local texture = state.textures[index]
			if texture ~= "" then state.textureTarget[state.textureProp] = texture end
			return
		end
		local frame = state.frames[index]
		local currentTexture = visual.TextureID
		visual:ApplyMesh(frame)
		if frame.TextureID == "" and currentTexture ~= "" then visual.TextureID = currentTexture end
	end)
end

-- Steps the sequence until the particle is reclaimed (or, for clones, the wall-clock cap).
local function runTask(pData, state, lifetime, liveSource)
	local startTime = os.clock()
	task.spawn(function()
		while not state.stopped do
			local visual = pData.VisualPart
			if not visual or not visual.Parent then break end
			if pData._nestedAlive and not pData._nestedAlive[1] then break end
			-- Its play has ended and its copy lives on as a Reactor: the mesh it shows stays.
			if pData._handedOver then return end
			if not liveSource and os.clock() - startTime > lifetime * 4 then break end
			local elapsed = pData._effectiveElapsed or (os.clock() - startTime)
			local frameIndex = MeshFlipMod.frameIndex(state, elapsed, pData.LifeTime or lifetime)
			if frameIndex ~= state.lastFrame then
				state.lastFrame = frameIndex
				applyFrame(state, visual, frameIndex)
			end
			task.wait()
		end
		if state.stopped or liveSource or state.mode == "Loop" or state.mode == "PingPong" then return end
		local visual = pData.VisualPart
		if visual and visual.Parent then applyFrame(state, visual, MeshFlipMod.finalFrame(state)) end
	end)
end

-- A pooled clone may still carry the previous emit's last frame: put the template's mesh back.
local function resetToTemplate(visualPart, specialMesh, rt)
	if not rt then return end
	if specialMesh then
		local rtMesh = rt:FindFirstChildOfClass("SpecialMesh")
		if rtMesh and specialMesh.MeshId ~= rtMesh.MeshId then pcall(function() specialMesh.MeshId = rtMesh.MeshId end) end
	elseif rt:IsA("MeshPart") and visualPart.MeshId ~= rt.MeshId then
		pcall(function() visualPart:ApplyMesh(rt) end)
	end
end

-- Bind the sequence to the visual: show the start frame now, then step it on the particle's clock.
-- liveSource = Animate on the RT itself: keep a backup for restore() and never time-cap the task.
function MeshFrames.attach(pData, data, visualPart, lifetime, liveSource)
	pData.MeshFrames = nil
	local active = isActive(data)
	local specialMesh = (not visualPart:IsA("MeshPart")) and visualPart:FindFirstChildOfClass("SpecialMesh") or nil
	if not visualPart:IsA("MeshPart") and not specialMesh then
		if active and not warnedUnsupported then
			warnedUnsupported = true
			Log.warn(("[Part-Icles] Mesh Frames need a MeshPart or a Part with a SpecialMesh as RenderTemplate; %s is a %s."):format(
				visualPart:GetFullName(), visualPart.ClassName))
		end
		return
	end
	if not active then
		if not liveSource then resetToTemplate(visualPart, specialMesh, data.RenderTemplate) end
		return
	end
	local state = buildState(data, visualPart)
	if specialMesh then
		state.specialMesh = specialMesh
		state.textureTarget, state.textureProp = textureSlot(visualPart, specialMesh)
	end
	if liveSource then
		if specialMesh then
			state.backup = { meshId = specialMesh.MeshId, texture = state.textureTarget[state.textureProp] }
		else
			local backup = visualPart:Clone()
			for _, child in ipairs(backup:GetChildren()) do child:Destroy() end
			backup.Name = "_MeshFrameBackup"
			backup.Archivable = false
			backup.Parent = VisualHost.getPoolFolder()
			state.backup = backup
		end
	end
	pData.MeshFrames = state
	runTask(pData, state, lifetime, liveSource)
end

-- Animate finish / cancel: stop stepping and put the RT's own mesh (and texture) back.
function MeshFrames.restore(pData)
	local state = pData.MeshFrames
	if not state then return end
	state.stopped = true
	local backup = state.backup
	if not backup then return end
	state.backup = nil
	local visual = pData.VisualPart
	if state.specialMesh then
		pcall(function()
			state.specialMesh.MeshId = backup.meshId
			state.textureTarget[state.textureProp] = backup.texture
		end)
		return
	end
	if visual and visual.Parent then pcall(function() visual:ApplyMesh(backup) end) end
	pcall(function() backup:Destroy() end)
end

-- AnimateLoop cycle: re-read the settings and frames for the next cycle.
function MeshFrames.refresh(pData, freshData)
	local state = pData.MeshFrames
	if not state or not freshData or not isActive(freshData) then return end
	local fresh = buildState(freshData, state.target)
	state.frames, state.n, state.mode = fresh.frames, fresh.n, fresh.mode
	state.meshIds, state.textures = fresh.meshIds, fresh.textures
	state.frameDelay, state.startOffset, state.reverse = fresh.frameDelay, fresh.startOffset, fresh.reverse
	state.lastFrame = -1
end

return MeshFrames

--[[
	NativeMotion  -  the path of one particle of a native ParticleEmitter, as the engine moves it.
	Every step the engine adds Acceleration to the particle's velocity and scales the whole
	velocity by 2 ^ (-Drag * dt). Drag is therefore a half-life (after 1 / Drag seconds half the
	speed is left), and it acts on Acceleration's share too: a falling particle approaches a
	terminal velocity. With k = ln(2) * Drag that is v' = a - k v, whose solution is
	  offset(t) = v0 * velocityShare + a * accelerationShare
	  velocityShare     = (1 - e^(-k t)) / k
	  accelerationShare = (t - velocityShare) / k
	and, for k = 0, velocityShare = t and accelerationShare = t^2 / 2.
	  NativeMotion.shares(drag, t) -> velocityShare, accelerationShare
	Plain numbers; the caller multiplies its own vectors. A negative Drag grows the speed.
	NOT the plugin's own particles: theirs is the same half-life on the Speed graph alone,
	Acceleration undragged (Part/DragModel).
	Consumer: Modules/MotionPreview (drawForPE).
]]

local NativeMotion = {}

local LN2 = math.log(2)
-- Below this k * t the drag terms cancel to nothing in floating point: the drag-free path is exact enough.
local NO_DRAG = 1e-6

function NativeMotion.shares(drag, t)
	local k = LN2 * drag
	if math.abs(k * t) < NO_DRAG then
		return t, t * t / 2
	end
	local velocityShare = (1 - math.exp(-k * t)) / k
	return velocityShare, (t - velocityShare) / k
end

return NativeMotion

--[[
	NestedEmit - source-walk dispatcher for nested transformed Part-Icles.

	Walks SOURCE RenderTemplate (never clones nested-source subtrees). Each
	transformed leaf fires via particle:EnableEmit with link=clonedRoot, which
	EmitPart's link branch consumes for both initial spawn pose and per-frame
	tracking. parentAlive cancels nested closures on parent pData reclaim.
]]

local Pool = require(script.Parent.Pool)
local Constants = require(script.Parent.PartConstants)

local NestedEmit = {}

-- Nearest ancestor with a world frame (BasePart / Attachment / Model / Bone), stopping at the RT root.
local function nearestFrameAncestor(node, sourceRT)
	local cur = node.Parent
	while cur and cur ~= sourceRT do
		if cur:IsA("BasePart") or cur:IsA("Attachment") or cur:IsA("Model") then return cur end
		cur = cur.Parent
	end
	return sourceRT
end

-- Walk source RT, fire each Transformed leaf. scaleNode (optional) is the parent-Model scale
-- chain node every leaf inherits as descCtx.ParentScale: a Model passes its own node, a
-- Part/Attachment forwards the node it inherited. _parentCloneMap forwards Pool's
-- source-to-clone map so nested Trail/Beam can rebind Attachment0/1.
-- _linkLocal is the leaf's parent-node offset from the RT root, so a leaf under a Model sub-part
-- spawns and tracks at that sub-part (LinkCF applies it to every link frame); nil at the root, which
-- keeps depth-1 children of a Part RT spawning at the clone itself. _sourceParentCF lets the spawn
-- rotation compose relative to that parent node instead of doubling the parent's world rotation.
-- decorate(node, descCtx), optional, runs last on every leaf's context: a Container hands each
-- leaf its drive record and its own place (keepPlace) there. _containerDrive is forwarded to
-- deeper leaves, so what a carried item carries shares its record; so is _matte (Matte/init).
-- _rigPlace (keepPlace) is never forwarded: what a carried item carries starts on its copy.
function NestedEmit.walk(particle, sourceRT, clonedRoot, parentAlive, emitCtx, scaleNode, decorate)
	if parentAlive and parentAlive[1] == false then return end
	local parentCloneMap = Pool._cloneMaps and Pool._cloneMaps[clonedRoot]
	-- Chain to the grandparent's map so a leaf resolves attachments authored one level up.
	-- Pool hits reuse the map, so the chain is refreshed rather than set once.
	local grandMap = emitCtx and emitCtx._parentCloneMap
	if parentCloneMap and grandMap and grandMap ~= parentCloneMap then
		local mt = getmetatable(parentCloneMap)
		if mt then mt.__index = grandMap else setmetatable(parentCloneMap, { __index = grandMap }) end
	end
	local leaves = {}
	local function visit(node)
		if node:GetAttribute("Transformed") then
			leaves[#leaves + 1] = node
			return
		end
		for _, child in node:GetChildren() do visit(child) end
	end
	visit(sourceRT)
	if #leaves == 0 then return end
	local rootCF = Constants.resolveLinkCFrame(sourceRT)
	local function fire(node)
		local descCtx = { ParentScale = scaleNode }
		local parentNode = nearestFrameAncestor(node, sourceRT)
		local parentCF = (parentNode == sourceRT) and rootCF or Constants.resolveLinkCFrame(parentNode)
		descCtx._sourceParentCF = parentCF
		if parentNode ~= sourceRT then descCtx._linkLocal = rootCF:ToObjectSpace(parentCF) end
		if emitCtx then
			descCtx.ChainCtx  = emitCtx.ChainCtx
			descCtx.EmitIndex = emitCtx.EmitIndex
			descCtx.EmitCount = emitCtx.EmitCount
			-- Forward the ghost play token so nested particles belong to the same play
			-- (PlayHandle:Disable / SetTimescale / GetParticles reach them too).
			descCtx._playToken = emitCtx._playToken
			descCtx._containerDrive = emitCtx._containerDrive
			descCtx._matte = emitCtx._matte
		end
		descCtx._parentAlive = parentAlive
		descCtx._parentCloneMap = parentCloneMap
		if decorate then decorate(node, descCtx) end
		particle:EnableEmit(node, clonedRoot, descCtx)
	end
	-- Attachment emitters first: EmitAttachment registers its visual in the map, so sibling
	-- Beams / Trails fired in the same walk bind their ends to the emitted attachment, and
	-- stock Beams / Trails in the parent copy are bound as each attachment registers.
	for _, node in ipairs(leaves) do
		if node:IsA("Attachment") then fire(node) end
	end
	for _, node in ipairs(leaves) do
		if not node:IsA("Attachment") then fire(node) end
	end
end


-- Gives a leaf its own place under the root: its link offset becomes its own frame in the
-- RenderTemplate (walk's default is its parent node's), so it spawns and tracks where it was
-- placed. A leaf with no frame of its own (a light, a beam) stays on its parent node.
-- _rigPlace is that place for the types that read no _linkLocal: a debris burst
-- (Rocks/PDataBuilder), a bolt (Lightning/PDataBuilder), a rope (Rope/PDataBuilder) and, by its
-- position alone, a camera shake and a screen distortion (CameraShake/init, Distortion/init).
-- Called from a Container's and a Matte's decorate.
function NestedEmit.keepPlace(node, descCtx, sourceRT)
	if not (node:IsA("BasePart") or node:IsA("Attachment") or node:IsA("Model")) then
		return
	end
	local own = Constants.resolveLinkCFrame(node)
	descCtx._linkLocal = Constants.resolveLinkCFrame(sourceRT):ToObjectSpace(own)
	descCtx._rigPlace = descCtx._linkLocal
	-- LinkCF.spawnFrame adds the leaf's rotation relative to this frame: none, the offset holds it.
	descCtx._sourceParentCF = own
end

-- Clone-side parent for a nested visual: the parent's copyBare clone of the source's nearest
-- BasePart ancestor, else the parent clone root when it is a BasePart. nil when not nested-driven
-- or nothing suitable was cloned (rig parents build per-segment copies and keep no map).
-- Consumer: EmitAttachment (visual parent). Keeps emitted visuals inside the parent
-- clone instead of the source RenderTemplate, where a later copyBare would template them.
function NestedEmit.resolveCloneParent(sourceNode, link, emitCtx)
	if not emitCtx then return nil end
	local map = emitCtx._parentCloneMap
	if map then
		local node = sourceNode.Parent
		while node and node ~= workspace do
			local clone = map[node]
			if clone then
				if clone:IsA("BasePart") then return clone end
				break
			end
			node = node.Parent
		end
	end
	if emitCtx._parentAlive and link and link:IsA("BasePart") then return link end
	return nil
end

return NestedEmit

--[[
	NestedScale  -  what an emitted copy holds, kept to the scale of the Model it is nested in.

	A Model's Scale reaches the plain things in its own copy through Model:ScaleTo. A mesh or
	an Attachment nested in that Model is a play of its own: the Model's factor sizes it and
	scales its motion (UpdatePart, UpdateAttachment), and this module does the same for what
	its copy holds, which Transform moved into its RenderTemplate: the Attachments, set apart
	by the factor, and the plain Beams between them (widths, curve sizes, segments, and the
	texture's length when the Model's Scale Texture is on).

	  NestedScale.textureScales(beam) -> boolean
	      TextureLength is studs a repeat in Wrap and Static, and a count of repeats along the
	      whole beam in Stretch, which a scale leaves alone. UpdateBeam asks it for a nested
	      Beam's own visual.
	  NestedScale.start(visual, parentScale, factor) -> record or nil
	      at the emit of a nested Part or Attachment, before its copy is parented. nil when
	      the copy holds nothing to scale.
	  NestedScale.apply(record, factor)
	      every frame from the update; writes only when the factor moved.
	  NestedScale.restore(record)
	      before the copy returns to the pool (LifecycleRelease._releaseVisual), so the next
	      play finds it as it was copied.

	Mutates a CLONE only: start is called from EmitPart and EmitAttachment, never from the
	Animate emits, whose visual is the live RenderTemplate.
	The scale a copy is made at. An Animate Model plays its live RenderTemplate and its ScaleTo
	scales the templates inside it (measured in Studio, 2026-10-12: attachments on parts, in
	folders and on attachments, beams, and the Scale of a Model nested in it), so a copy of
	one comes out at the Model's scale of that moment: what it holds is scaled from there.
	Under a Model that emits a copy a template is never scaled. The copy keeps that scale as
	the attribute _copiedScale (RESERVED_ATTRS.md), because a pooled copy is taken again when
	the live Model stands at another scale.
	A part or a model inside the copy is not moved, so what it holds is left with it.
	A Container that carries the copy writes its Beams' widths every frame and has the last word.
]]

local NestedScale = {}

function NestedScale.textureScales(beam)
	return beam.TextureMode ~= Enum.TextureMode.Stretch
end

-- The scale `visual` was copied at: the scale of the nearest Model above that plays its live
-- RenderTemplate, 1 when every Model above emits a copy.
local function copiedAt(visual, parentScale)
	local kept = visual:GetAttribute("_copiedScale")
	if kept then
		return kept
	end
	local node = parentScale
	while node do
		local owner = node.Owner
		if owner and owner.IsAnimate then
			local live = owner.VisualPart
			if live and live.Parent then
				return math.max(live:GetScale(), 0.001)
			end
			return 1
		end
		node = node.Parent
	end
	return 1
end

-- Lists the Attachments and Beams under `holder`, with what they are now.
local function collect(holder, record)
	for _, child in ipairs(holder:GetChildren()) do
		if child:GetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit") then
			-- Another play's visual, placed by its own update.
			continue
		end
		if child:IsA("Attachment") then
			table.insert(record.attachments, child)
			table.insert(record.positions, child.Position)
			collect(child, record)
		elseif child:IsA("Beam") then
			table.insert(record.beams, child)
			table.insert(record.shapes, {
				width0 = child.Width0,
				width1 = child.Width1,
				curveSize0 = child.CurveSize0,
				curveSize1 = child.CurveSize1,
				segments = child.Segments,
				textureLength = (record.scaleTexture and NestedScale.textureScales(child)) and child.TextureLength or nil,
			})
		elseif not (child:IsA("BasePart") or child:IsA("Model")) then
			collect(child, record)
		end
	end
end

function NestedScale.start(visual, parentScale, factor)
	if not parentScale then
		return nil
	end
	local copied = copiedAt(visual, parentScale)
	local record = {
		copied = copied,
		factor = copied,
		scaleTexture = parentScale.ScaleTextureLength ~= false,
		attachments = {},
		positions = {},
		beams = {},
		shapes = {},
	}
	collect(visual, record)
	if #record.attachments == 0 and #record.beams == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	if copied ~= 1 then
		visual:SetAttribute("_copiedScale", copied)
	end
	NestedScale.apply(record, factor)
	return record
end

function NestedScale.apply(record, factor)
	if factor == record.factor then
		return
	end
	record.factor = factor
	-- What the copy holds was read at the scale it was copied at.
	local grown = factor / record.copied
	local positions = record.positions
	for index, attachment in ipairs(record.attachments) do
		attachment.Position = positions[index] * grown
	end
	local shapes = record.shapes
	for index, beam in ipairs(record.beams) do
		local shape = shapes[index]
		beam.Width0 = shape.width0 * grown
		beam.Width1 = shape.width1 * grown
		beam.CurveSize0 = shape.curveSize0 * grown
		beam.CurveSize1 = shape.curveSize1 * grown
		-- A longer curve takes more segments; never fewer than it was copied with.
		beam.Segments = math.max(shape.segments, math.round(shape.segments * grown))
		if shape.textureLength then
			beam.TextureLength = shape.textureLength * grown
		end
	end
end

function NestedScale.restore(record)
	NestedScale.apply(record, record.copied)
end

return NestedScale

--[[
	Orientation Mixin  -  per-frame rotation overlay for Part / Model / Attachment.
	Modes mirror ParticleOrientation: None, FacingCamera, FacingCameraWorldUp,
	VelocityParallel, VelocityPerpendicular. Composes as `orient * existingRotation`.
	ApplyZOffset runs after this and keeps the rotation written here (ZOffset.luau).
]]
